# On the Formation of the Human Being

Death, which cannot be called life, is like a death in this state, adding to it that wind <note>original: "ventum"; likely referring to the *pneuma* or vital spirit</note> while sleeping, which is not present when in the fourth month it strengthens those winds with the senses. Those winds will remain in the heart with the soul; therefore, when that wind strengthens over the soul, it will give life to the body. The soul will strengthen over the wind, and the wind will strengthen over our seed while sleeping. Thus, there is a division by change according to whether the wind strengthens over one thing or another, appearing with different effects. All three common [winds] sometimes desert their light, while others do not. The seventh wind remains from the seed until the third month arrives, which is called the "first sound."

Then follows the third and fourth [months], and it is full of blood.

**Concerning the third month in which the seventh [wind] is said to be received**
The wind goes to our seed, and according to the color of the world, the flesh is born and becomes coagulated in the manner of blood. It gains weight, and the seventh wind hides itself from the vessel <note>the womb</note> like a monk. That wind [departs] from the body, and those vessels which it held remain; it sends a second [force], and they remain in that nest, purifying everything until the fourth month arrives.

**Concerning the 4th month**
And then it is placed in disposition. All three [winds] prevail according to that strength, and the light in which it changed them will remain. The wind, as a changed thing, prevails in all its strength and will give—**it is said**—it will give the soul to it. The soul will be fulfilled in it according to the time; the veins will appear in it, and likewise the openings and the form of a human.

**In the fifth month it conceives, in which the ninth [wind] is said to be**
And then the wind—it is said—at the fourth month, which becomes the form, therefore the shapes of the members appear in it. Their hair is born, and it increases according to the preparation of that month.

**Concerning the sixth month of conception, in which the Lord [rules]**
And after, it will change in the sixth month, and it is disposed, which is full of sweat and the change of bodies. Now its tongue and its members descend and prevail in the mother with the limbs and feet. It will strengthen the movement and does not want the narrowness of the place; it seeks to go from the darkness of the womb to the world, and it is thus prepared in that nest.

**In the seventh month it conceives, in which the third [wind] is said to be**
And after the seventh month, the wind—it is said—goes to the third, and the form is completed and strengthened with strength. The members—it is said—are born in that month with the movement of the organs <note>original: "splanchna" (Greek for internal organs)</note>, and it will have trust in life and soul, and thus they remain.

**Concerning the eighth month in which the seventh [wind] returns**
In the eighth, the wind—it is said—goes to the seventh; it will strengthen and block <note>or "oppress"</note> according to the coldness, and it will remain in it through the eighth month to be nourished. If it is born in that eighth month, it is born [weak] and its movement is congealed. The wind—it is said—goes to the seventh, and when it is perceived, it was not willing. To one whom God wished to give mercy, it pleased [God]; but he to whom God wished to give death does not live. It moves, and the birth occurs—it is said—the birth of humans and beasts without pressure, with the mother's members... <note>The text here becomes a complex astrological calculation involving the "house of the sun" (Leo) and the "exaltation of the sun" (Aries).</note>

**Concerning the signs by which the movement of the child in the womb is signified**
Now the movement of the child in the mother's womb is according to the quantity in which it is shown by the signs. For the born child, they foreknow the members with the Lord [of the sign] and with the exaltation, which is from Leo (the house of the Sun) to Aries (the exaltation). These are the nine signs with this sign, with the month and the world... at the hour of birth. They consider the prelations, the angles, and the Lord of the house, and how the zodiac will be in the water of life. We shall foreknow what will be first and what the stars signify when the seed is cast into the womb. God is in some of the signs of the Sun, illuminating from the hour of the first fall into the womb until the hour of its progress from the mother's womb.

By this change, it exits the womb and is placed from [stage to stage] until it exits to the sign in the place where it was when it began. It is true that they are perceived through the [four] signs: Fire, Air, Earth, and Water. The wind [corresponds] to the nature of the sign in which it is conceived. This is in the fifth month... the members are incarnated by Water, and the spirit of the child is according to the nature of the signs, whether Fire or Water, indicating strength or defect.

# On additions, subtractions, and complexions made, and the distance, and the appetite, and the child being born, and the teeth and upper parts.

### In what way the infant, having been conceived, is completed in the womb
<margin>Secondly, that which is said</margin>

It should be known that in the womb there is a leading of all things over the <term>guma</term><note>likely a corruption of 'gemma' or 'gumma', referring to the vital sap or formative substance</note> and the wretched mass, and it is placed upon the bitterness and rendered to be embittered; and that which is the great umbilical cord is wondrous, and they say there is something else in the womb in which it is directed and nourished. And there is the chewing and the juice of the vessels to the veins of the womb, so that they might be its own; from the bones to the belly of the mother. Therefore, when the chewing has gone out from nature to the mixture made, this to that, and because there is a delay from one part of the womb into the womb, nor is there movement from that motion and rest until it comes to the head, to its own place where it is able. And it has strength, as it is said, it goes out from a narrow place—namely from the vulva—into the world, and it is constricted and outside of here it is weighed down and suffers pain on account of the curvature and the impulse of the wind <note>referring to the 'pneuma' or vital breath/gas believed to aid birth</note>; and the seed is fled from the exit at the hour of the fall of the mother. 

And when it shall go out, it must be restrained with the eyes toward the light of the sun if by day, or to the light of a candle by night; and it breathes toward the light and changes, for the eyes are changed in a way that is in the beginning, which was not before; and by its goodness which it did not have from nature, it preserves the senses of the womb in the heart, to which it is mixed. You shall see in the one born on the day of his birth, that when the day of birth [comes], he tends with his hands toward the sufferings of the mother and of all those things which God gave. And this is the first thing that disposes the world, acting toward the finger of the great brain of the marrow; and he who struggles with the marrow is brought to me, and it is given by God from above, and it is made of that which offends him, and since it is from him, he sends him. And you will see in the world that this mystery has been made for me, and the world was first to see the movement toward it when the first fruit <note>original: "pomum", literally apple/fruit, here likely the fetus</note> moves to weeping; and when from there it was first to rejoice and grieve and weep, like one who preserves the water in the hand of the Lord over the heads of them. ### Concerning the maker of the first month and how it is now governed by its own lord

And from this, observe these three places: if they look upon each other by aspect <note>In astrology, an "aspect" is a specific angular relationship between planets or points, such as a trine or square</note>, the delay of the birth in the mother's womb will be for as many months as the birth-chart promises. <margin>Saturn</margin>
Saturn is the maker of the first month from the fall of the seeding. And if he is strong in the horoscope, both in his exaltation and in his term or in his own house <note>The "house" or "domicile" is the zodiac sign a planet naturally rules; for Saturn, this is Capricorn or Aquarius</note>, that seed is gentle and will gain many things; [though] losses from pain and sickness may harm it, yet that seed is raised to the upper parts of the belly. There is much water and the water is very beautiful <unclear>and</unclear> it is in fear <unclear>and</unclear> there is joy for many in her pregnancy. She thinks good thoughts and shows many people everything she has regarding that pregnancy; she is healthy in her whole body and of good spirit, being well-disposed. And regarding that which is in the belly—the water—it shows the likeness of that pregnancy to be good <unclear>and</unclear> in fear on account of the finding of many sorrowful spirits and sickness and the changing of the body. They see a bite of blood in the hand of the pregnancy, and she regards it sorrowfully in the lower part of the belly, and the pregnancy is fit for all. And if [Saturn] is in the lowest point, she is happy for many reasons and the seed is healthy; she will have strength and health and increase in that pregnancy, and its color is beautiful, and she hungers for beauty and righteousness and an increase of beauty through itself in fear. Or if he is in his greater house, it is very gentle in the term of pregnancy, and she rejoices with many messages, though few [unclear] spirits are found; the pregnancy does not show itself with change, and there is a memory of the month and the day of the pregnancy, and the day of the pregnancy was the same as the day of the water. # Concerning the significator of the month because it is Mercury ☿

The Moon ☽ cannot endure being joined by anything lower than herself; she is the author of all actions and births and does not rest from taking vengeance on enemies and evil thoughts. <meta>This page continues the discussion of astrological influences on the human body, specifically focusing on the physical characteristics (physiognomy) granted to those born under the influence of the seven planets and the twelve signs of the zodiac.</meta>

### On the properties of Jupiter and what he gives to those born under him

He is curly-haired <note>original: "Crispus"</note> with white skin and has shaggy hair. Jupiter is said to be white and reddish-black; he has large eyes in proportion to his own size, neither red nor flat but moderate; a curly beard; handsome in his own way; the head and jaws are somewhat elevated; a large nose, even in flesh; his stature is balanced; his speech is sweet with cheerfulness.

### On the properties of Mars

He is ruddy <note>original: "Ruffus"</note> with red skin, having white, round eyes; the face and head all tend toward whiteness; for if by chance they have red spots <note>original: "mofetas rubeas," likely referring to skin blemishes or birthmarks</note> and a large face, he will have full eyes in the face; the nose is entirely long, large, sharp, and thin; black, yet often handsome in its straightness; the face is swollen, sad, and prone to evil speech; with a "red" <note>likely meaning angry or heated</note> manner of speaking; his fingers are a little long; striking everyone with his flesh in his gait; he is of long weight in his heart, mind, and countenance; in thought he always speaks evil.

### On the properties of the Sun and what he gives to those born under him

The Sun is white, of great whiteness; the eyes are small and round; the face and head are large; his color is intense; flat hair; a broad forehead; his eyes are properly tinged with red; his stature is measured in the body, but in spirit, shame <note>original: "vicundia," likely *verecundia*</note> appears; with a "red" <note>heated or authoritative</note> manner of speech.

### On the properties of Venus

Venus is white, shining, and pleasant; a reddish tint appears in the eyes; she shows beautiful eyes and is delightful, like a glowing red; her hair is curly; the blackness of the eyes is greater than the whiteness; proper spaces; roundness of the head; straight, pleasant eyebrows; everything is subtle and small; long jaws; and the whiteness of the eyes is properly tending toward blackness.

### On the properties of Mercury

Mercury is white tending toward greenness; he has a narrow forehead; his jaw is drawn back; the pupils <note>original: "cora"</note> have pleasant spaces; long nostrils; a wide mouth, mobile in every way; small teeth; a thin, hairy beard; the face and fingers are thin; they are small, but his better parts are subtle; much flesh, but many good qualities of his own.

### On the properties of the Moon

The Moon is white with a round face; she appears decorous and soft; a beautiful beard <note>Note: In medieval astrology, the Moon's "beard" may refer to facial texture or a masculine personification</note>; a clear color; a healthy body filled with limbs; sweet speech; but her manner is specifically and friendly in a phlegmatic way <note>term: phlegmatic - one of the four humors, associated with water, coolness, and a calm or stolid temperament</note>; because the air is measured through wisdom, then such signs are proper to those born of me.

### On the properties of Aries

Aries has much hair, is curly, tending toward whiteness; ruddy with red; a long face; he has large eyes; a small front and a large neck.

### On the properties of Taurus and what he gives to the one born

Taurus has a broad forehead and long fingers; a nose with wide nostrils; large, open eyes; his hair is ruddy and moderate; with the upper fingers over a thick neck; strong blackness of the hair; he is likewise delighted in his gait.

### On the properties of Gemini and what he gives to the one born in that place

Gemini is of equal stature; a broad chest; confident and strong; he is a writer and a calculator <note>note: Gemini was traditionally associated with Mercury and intellectual/clerical professions</note>.

### On the properties of Cancer

Cancer is pale and ruddy; straight in limbs; a straight nose; the limbs are smaller and drawn back in their own way.

### On the properties of Leo

Leo has a large forehead; turned-back teeth; curly hair and a short beard; small stature; large, human eyes.

### On the properties of Virgo and what she confers to the one born

Virgo has flaming hair; large eyes; her stature is proper and beautiful; the upper limbs are larger; a broad chest; red nostrils; the eyes are a little red in likeness; a grave face; bad in cleanliness <note>original: "obmundine," likely *immundine*</note>.

### On the properties of Libra and what she gives to the one born

Libra has a beautiful stature and her limbs are handsome at the limit of nature.

### On the properties of Scorpio

Scorpio's stature is handsome in flesh, height, and manner.

### On the properties of Sagittarius

Sagittarius is white; hair like flaming wheels; long, thick neck; a long face and the beard is handsomer behind; his hair is subtle; a large belly.

### On the properties of Capricorn and what he gives much to the one born

Capricorn has a subtle neck and thus a sluggish face; with threads that are red; his beard is sharp; he has much hair.

### On the properties of Aquarius

Aquarius is of short stature; a friend to the great and more tamed among sweet men; many depart with little grace; a straight countenance; one hand or the other; blood appears with red.

### On the properties of Pisces and what he gives to his own born under him

Pisces, however, has a broad chest; a small, heavy head; a beard; his jaws are broad; white; evil in mind; and he is called the sign of the "ascender" through his signs; those who are born then have a large and handsome body; the ascending sign is for those who are born with their own body.

They were born according to that which is constant.

### Concerning the newborn who is born and nourished but does not reach old age

<margin>Short life</margin>

**A**fter the aforementioned chapter, since the newborn does not reach old age, we must first speak of the significations of the Sun and Jupiter. Therefore, they have the information of that birth in those places taken from the fortunates and unfortunates. From Jupiter it flows in because Jupiter is in the Tenth House and in a good place, and has primary strength if the Sun is the lord of it from a fortunate youth. And if it is held by the unfortunates, as the stars indicate, give the newborn a short life. Truly, if Jupiter is in a good place, it signifies the delay <note>stay/duration</note> of the newborn in the world. If the fortunes are masculine as they appear to the ascendant by aspect, the newborn is guarded.

If Jupiter is in the angles, such as in the points of the angles, and that power appears from misfortune and is indicated by retrogrades and combustion <note>term: combustion; when a planet is so close to the Sun that its power is "burned up"</note>, the newborn overcomes and is nourished. From the Sun and Jupiter in the ascendant, the newborn overcomes the world because the Sun and Moon are free from misfortunes and destruction, because they are not peregrine <note>term: peregrine; a planet in a position where it has no essential dignity or strength</note>. And the ascendant flows into the house in exaltation or in the middle degrees, and they are not retrograde nor unfortunate in the change, and greater because they are in their exaltation. And it is said more because they are in all fortune. And the lords of the light of the newborn are unfortunate, yet Jupiter brings nourishment, especially in the ascendant, because he is above the limit and because he is masculine or in a prominent place. The lord of the place of fortune, appearing with its rays, signifies the stay of the newborn and that he is nourished. And if the newborn is protected by the lord in the night, and Jupiter is in the angle of the ascendant, it is a good fortune and a long duration for the newborn.

# On the Knowledge of the Giver of Life

"Knowing life and death," says <unclear>Albedeni</unclear> <note>Likely Al-Battani, a famous 9th-century Arab astronomer/astrologer</note>, "you should build wisely and discern wisely."
Determine the **Givers of Life** <term>vites: likely a Latinization of the Arabic 'Haylaj' (Hyleg), the planet or point that signifies the life force</term> from five places: from the **day** and the **degree of the day**, from the **Ascendant** of fortune, and the **oriental sign** <note>the sign rising on the eastern horizon</note>, so that it may be foreseen.
If they are before the birth, the **Givers of Life** for those born in the day are in the fourth [house] from the **Sun**, graduated further; and for those [born at night], from the **Moon** of the day. The **Givers of Life**, if it is a nocturnal birth, are in the fourth from the **Moon** and the **degree** of the night. The **Givers of Life**, if it is in the rising birth and joined either in the **seventh** or in the **tenth house**, if the **sign** of fortune be a masculine or feminine sign. And the **Giver of Life**, if its lord appears as its Giver of Life, or the **Moon** in its **exaltation** or **triplicity** <note>technical terms for signs where a planet has specific strengths</note>. Then, if that lord of the Giver of Life does not appear, it is not the Giver of Life.
If the lord is not in its proper places and **Mars** is in the **seventh**, **eighth**, or **nona** [ninth house], and it was a masculine sign, it will be the Giver of Life, unless those who behold that lord of the Giver of Life are **fortunes** <note>benefic planets like Jupiter or Venus</note>. Therefore, the Giver of Life is that which appears in the **Alcocoden** <term>Alkokoden: the planet that determines the length of life based on the Hyleg's position</term> in the same way for those born at night as in the day. And if the **Moon** is in the midheaven or in the **ninth**, or in the **august** [majestic] places, or in the twelfth, third, seventh, or ninth, and is in a sign, it acts as the Giver of Life itself, which should behold the **Alcocoden**. And if you find the Giver of Life nearby, which beholds it for good fortune or misfortunes, and it was in the house of the **Giver of Life**, if the lord is not in this, do not look to the Giver of Life. Joined, if it is free from defect and the lord of the union is strong and free from an angle <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</note> or from the **succeeding** angles, neither retrograde nor falling nor **conjoined**, the union is the Giver of Life, and from that, the Giver of Life is most highly taken.
If the union is not the Giver of Life, look through the places of the **Giver of Life**; if it is found either in the **succeeding** angles and is free from misfortunes so that its part appears, the lord of the Giver of Life is of the **exaltation** or the **Moon** or the **triplicity**. And the Giver of Life and the part and the **Alcocoden** appear, and then the union was the Giver of Life more so; look into it. And if it is not so, look to the **Giver of Life** as you were cautioned, which presides over the birth of the native. If the **Moon** is an impediment, the part of the Giver of Life is no more joined through all of them. And if the Giver of Life was as we said in the generation of the giver, before it comes to misfortunes so that the fortune of the Giver of Life does not appear, the **birth** in that year—and certain wise men said that the Giver of Life itself was not the Giver of Life—let the **Giver of Life** appear if it was in the day in an angle or the midheaven. If the Giver of Life has any power either in the union in the sign of fortune, it is the Giver of Life for the degree of the manner and place in the birth in the fourth [house]. And in the day, the Giver of Life is in the angle of the earth <note>the 4th house/Imum Coeli</note> by **degrees**; it is the Giver of Life. And if it and the **Alcocoden** appear, namely the Giver of Life, it says that you will not find any part of the five wise [points] which are the Giver of Life. Look through the places which are in the union and its lord of fortune, and in which union and the **part of the Giver of Life** and the angles. And the Giver of Life itself is from the **degree** which goes out in the degree from the union into the unfortunate; it is certainly the Giver of Life, provided the lord be masculine in sign and is in the union and in its own house, or has no power. Or if the union and the lord in which the union sits is in the **seventh** and in the **ninth**, it will be worse for its house; they do not want fortunes nor the Giver of Life. If they are joined and through the places of fortune as previously mentioned, the Giver of Life should not appear for the born, whether it be a sign of fortune, or masculine, or whether it be of night or day, which is strong and free from misfortunes and from the life which all of their places show. The Giver of Life is that which you know as the union in the Giver of Life.
If the union was in and joined to the places of misfortune from the **Sun** or **Moon**, and if it does not come to misfortunes and there is no defect in its completed rays upon that place, then it is of that death. And if fortune appears or its completed rays to the place of misfortune, its completion is great and will liberate him from the **Giver of Life**. If the lord of the Giver of Life is not in the day, in the night look through the union if it is an **equational** birth; if indeed it is **proportional**, look through fortune and the union was from there. And so says **Ptolemy** <note>Claudius Ptolemy, the foundational authority for medieval astrology</note> that the Giver of Life is in that which is the union, if it be the Giver of Life to the union of fortunes and misfortunes. For he who falls into misfortunes, it shall be one of two things: either it brings evil to the daughter of death, or it admits misfortunes to him. And then he is born both of the Giver of Life and the union of misfortunes, and having completed to it in or in **misfortune** at the time of birth, death remains over the native. And if the union which is the Giver of Life is in the root of the birth, an unfortunate union, it will bind itself in one union or in its unfortunate **sign**, just as we showed in the union of the born; therefore he shall fear death from it, and he who was in the **sign** so that it may be found, fortune does not appear.

### On the Divider of Years

<margin>Years</margin>
It begins from the Lord of the Ascendant in that year and for each year, and it is unique according to the property of the primary <term>Causes</term> <note>original: "Caus", likely referring to the causal planetary influences</note> of each chapter. And these are the years from the <term>Moon</term> <note>original: "lunae"</note> which are pleasing, as it is necessary for a wise man in your operation; and before the primary [calculation], it leads into the canon of the table more than anything else. And note that it is said that the life of each person is in the shadows in the kingdom's governance, and it says that if one month is placed in fear, then those years will be greater. And if it begins from <term>Saturn</term>, it will be first. But if <term>Jupiter</term> shines, and if you multiply 10 by [the proper factor], it makes 120, and those are the "Great Years." And similarly, if <term>Mars</term> falls, you multiply 9 by 7 and the total becomes 108, and those are the "Lesser Years" of <term>Mars</term>. But for the "Middle Years" of <term>Jupiter</term> and <term>Saturn</term>, one takes the half of the greater ones, which is 60, and adds the years previously noted which are 10; that makes 60, and let it become 49 <note>The arithmetic here reflects specific astrological traditions where "years" are added or subtracted based on planetary dignity</note>, and take the half of them, which is 24 and a half, and those are the "Middle Years" of <term>Jupiter</term>. And he halved the years of <term>Saturn</term>, 250, and they are 150, and added to them the previous years which are 27, making 147; then he took the half of those, which is 74 and a half. The primary years of <term>Jupiter</term> and <term>Saturn</term> are 40. Now, if <term>Jupiter</term> aspects the month, <term>Mars</term> gives the planet to this galaxy which is in 19 degrees of Virgo; thus the primary years, if they are placed there, are 19 years. But the three times of the month, it is said, approach Andromeda until it comes to the wind, which is 24 days; and from that relief, the primary years are 27. But the primary years of <term>Venus</term> are 120 after the equal aspect to the water, because they are 20 days or as such. But the primary years of <term>Mercury</term> are 20 years... <term>Jupiter</term>... 12... because both months are the whole. But because they are 8, because now the months contain the matter in the <term>Moon</term>. And because the cause stands from the house of the wise according to the days, they are a sign of the night, but the months are indeed the primary years of the <term>Moon</term>, and it is from 18 to 20 years. But the "Middle Years" of the <term>Moon</term> are 12, and he took from the primary month and more, and thus it is the middle.

### On the Division of Years in a Nativity

Know that the "Divider of Years" in a birth <note>original: "nati", referring to the subject of a horoscope</note> is through the aspects in the Ascendant, however many cases there are in this, and you should take what remains from the first, from <term>Jupiter</term> in the Ascendant, as well as from the Lord of the [House] which disposes the years of the birth. If anything remains... it is necessary that we fear the governance of the body, only seven [planets] and the cases of others, and in the primary ones until the life of the newborn is completed. And calculate the planets aspecting the governance and their strength face to face with the face of the Lord of the [House]. And if both are present, it will unluckily affect his portion of death. And if both are unfortunate, it will unluckily affect his portion in death. ->On the Nature and Manners of the Born<-

It is the star of Jupiter and Saturn, and that which remains from the term of Jupiter, and there come two which remain with Jupiter in the <unclear>ascendant</unclear> according to the quantity of days where Saturn and Jupiter are joined. That defines what remained in the tenth of Saturn and Jupiter. Thus it is said that for the one born, they speak with a good tongue and are praised in the movement of the soul and heart. And when it is thus through Jupiter for the years and months from the birth, if Saturn and Jupiter provoke their rays upon that term, he will have for two years from his birth the same heat and pain from the heat of the hands, or strongly by blood or fire, according to the quantity of their Saturn and the aspects or destructions. And let it not be a sign in which time all Jupiter's conditions shall be made, and the rays shall provide for that term from Jupiter through the spirituality of the body... <note>The Latin here is highly abbreviated and technical, referring to "profections" or the movement of planetary influence over specific years of life.</note> and he who gives from good into evil by the motion of Jupiter when he operates in the term of Saturn, which I have divided and undivided in my measure to the term of Saturn from itself in Jupiter. And of Saturn it is said therefore that after 2 years and 10 months have passed, the life is fortunate and of good omen, and of a fortunate and good life, greatly adorned according to the providence and riches of Saturn. And Jupiter provokes his rays upon the lord of his places, whether in the 1st or 2nd year; whenever he aspects Saturn, he will have a nature of pain from [afflictions], and sometimes he will have pain in coldness or double and long fevers. Saturn makes evil or misfortune through the hours until the completion of the years and months with the disposition of Jupiter. Therefore, I found within both beauty and fitness of the body and joy in worldly things. And in the times of Saturn for 10 years, whatever the disposition of the fate of Jupiter may be, the one born shall first have much labor and old age, and shall have friendship with kings and with the wealth of riches and many [distances] and pains. And he shall have merit and an evil death which follows the disposition of Jupiter until the end. If Saturn then holds sway over that birth in labor and [distance], he shall invade him with fever and blood and malignancy of the body, and he shall not be fit for work and shall be very solitary. And if he has a wife or children, he shall grieve for them and proceed to a [failing] sign... until the end of the death of the one born.

->**On the foolishness of the one born**<-

Good counsel stands heavily against sensible actions. And when Jupiter is with masculine signs and Mercury is in the ascendant <note>original: "monte", likely referring to the rising sign or "mountain" of the house</note>, the one born will be subtle, filled with the highest intellect. And when all of Jupiter and Mercury are in the ascendant or in the house, the one born will be foolish, rather than being under a wise and prudent man. **On the ignorance and foolish presumption of the one born.** Know that when Jupiter is in the house of the Moon and looks toward the Sun, the one born is foolish. And when Jupiter and Venus are in the said Sun and Mercury is in the place of the Moon, the one born is foolish and is named by all for his foolishness, for he is one of those at whom men laugh. And when Venus and Mercury are masculine and the Moon is in their [orbit], the one born is foolish and contemptible. **On the one born who is an entertainer of kings and princes.** Know that when [a planet] is in the house of the sign of Saturn, the one born is an entertainer <note>original: "inferio", likely a minstrel or low-born jester</note>. And it is the sign in which Saturn and the Sun are the kingdom of kings, and the Sun looking upon him, the one born is an entertainer of kings and one with whom kings and princes rejoice because of his strength. And if the Sun and Saturn are in the manner of Mercury in a falling sign, know that the one born under Jupiter will be an entertainer of kings and one with whom Jupiter and the first of these laugh. And when Venus appears in Mercury in the ascendant with him, the one born is a friend of pleasant speech and men will marvel at him. And when either Saturn with Jupiter shall see these things from their strength, they will marvel; the one born under Jupiter in the house of Saturn and the Moon will be his friend, the one born will be an entertainer speaking eloquently and beautifully. **On the one born as a faithful guardian.** Know that when Jupiter is in the house with [the stars] by night and day and in the manner of the ascendant, the one born is faithful, in whom his master faithfully guards all things. And when with Jupiter in the Sun, the one born is faithful and the master and other sublime men trust in him. And when Jupiter and Mercury appear, and Jupiter does not appear [otherwise], the one born is a good and faithful savior of all. And when Venus is masculine and they rejoice with Jupiter, the one born is faithful and a savior of all. # On the worst nature of the sodomite <note>original: "De natu pessima sodomita"</note>

☉ ☽ ♃ ♄ ♂ ♀ ☿ <note>Symbols for Sun, Moon, Jupiter, Saturn, Mars, Venus, Mercury</note> If the Sun, Moon, and Jupiter are in the house where a "Gomorrite" <note>A historical term for a sodomite, referencing the biblical city of Gomorrah</note> is born, and Jupiter is in Aquarius or Pisces, or in any house where Jupiter is in its sign, the one born is an augur <note>a diviner or fortune-teller</note> and a Gomorrite.

### On the worst birth and other types of births

But if the Sun and Moon are in the midheaven <note>original: "cent meridie," the highest point in the sky at birth</note> in the births of women, that "evil work" of intercourse is said to occur which women do with women; and variously, when a woman acts as a male and <unclear>pe</unclear> in the birth of a woman, she is like a sailor in nature, or rather has the properties of a woman but cohabits with them <unclear>pe</unclear> on the part of the female or in her own Aquarius, which is in the place of the male, and with them a mixture of blood is born from a certain nature.
If it happens that Venus and Mercury are in <unclear>q q</unclear> through the south <unclear>m r</unclear> in that which is male in the midheaven, a woman is born and it is supposed she "broke herself" <note>likely a reference to a physical or moral rupture</note>; she is called an Argus. And if the Sun and Moon are in the midheaven by aspect and <unclear>p q</unclear>, then every person born will be a servant and <unclear>moes</unclear>, similarly having the manners of women, and he will be overcome by that womanliness which is found in Libra, a mixture of military service, such as is in Virgo and Gemini, or Taurus, Aries, and Capricorn; and the path of the Sun and Moon scrapes the brother, for he will be born among women and desires men. And if Jupiter is in the house of Jupiter, and Jupiter is in the house of Venus, or in the angles of the night in Leo or Virgo, the person is born to the "death of woman" <note>possibly meaning a loss of feminine virtue or a specific medical condition</note>, and when there is misfortune and lack of strength in the sign, he is born as if he were a woman, acts womanly, and seeks out men just as women do.

### On one born of good complexion and chaste

One born when Jupiter is in the sign of Jupiter was born chaste and of a good complexion; and he is chaste if Jupiter is in the midheaven, in the southern sky in Leo or in any of the houses of the virtues, and they cross the space and Jupiter does not look upon <note><term>aspect/look upon</term>: an astrological term for the geometric relationship between planets</note> the birth, he is a chaste philosopher, a creator of philosophy, and superstitious in his unions. And if it is in any of the houses of exaltation immediately from the birth, and Jupiter is in the midheaven, he is born a chaste prince—like Louis—generous from the fruits of virtue, profuse, liberal, and of good fame.

### On one born liberal, generous, and prodigal

One born in the part where Jupiter aspects Jupiter in the house <unclear>p m</unclear> is born liberal and generous, spending from his own means; or he may be prodigal if Jupiter aspects the Sun and Moon, having practiced humanity intact so that nothing remains of Jupiter. If the Sun is the lord of the father's fortune and the lord aspects from the end of the month, he is born prodigal. And if it happens that Jupiter is in Gemini by aspect at birth, he is predicted to become poor through his actions. And if the lord aspects every part of the present, the Sun is there, and he will be prodigal and have a blemish on his person.

### On one born greedy

One born when Saturn is the lord and is in aspect to the Sun, he is born [greedy]; and if Saturn is in the night rising in Aquarius by aspect, he will be greedy. And if the lord of Aquarius is in aspect by day, he is greedy. And if the lord aspects appearing according to Mercury from Taurus by aspect, he will be wonderfully greedy, a diligent and persistent brother.

### On one born mute

One born when Mercury is fast in the night is born mute; and if Mercury is perpetually in aspect and property <unclear>mue</unclear>, he is born mute. And if Mercury is in aspect and bound to the Sun and does not aspect the Moon, he will be born mute.

### On one born with a tongue-tie and who speaks much

One born when Mercury is in <unclear>tr</unclear> with the Moon or aspects it, he is born tongue-tied <note>original: "egoglossus," likely meaning a speech impediment or stammer</note>, they will cry out to him, and he adds to his words and speaks more. And if Mercury is in Gemini and aspects the Moon, he will be tongue-tied and speak for a long time and speak more. And if Mercury is in Aries and Gemini and Mercury is bound, he is born with great <unclear>velfindiis</unclear> without shame; if bound to the Moon by Saturn in the Sun or Moon, he is born greatly tongue-tied and [speaks to] the whole world.

### On one born cheerful, of good response, cautious, and a flatterer

One born when Jupiter is in aspect and aspects the part of Venus or Mercury is born cheerful, of good response, and a festive companion. And if Jupiter is in the midheaven or in aspect and Venus aspects it, he is born with a cheerful face, a flatterer, and of good speech. And if it is in aspect in its own face <note>a specific 10-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign</note> and Mercury aspects it from its own house, he is born without shame, a flatterer, and of good conversation. And if Jupiter and Mercury aspect Venus, he is born with a cheerful face and good at communication.

### On one born sad, of evil speech, and insane

One born with Saturn in many places in the births [is affected]. And if Saturn is in its own aspect, he is born sad, of evil speech, and insane. And if Saturn is the lord and makes an aspect and the Moon and Mercury aspect it in Capricorn or Aquarius, he is born sad in all things. And if Saturn is in the face in the head and does not aspect Venus, he is born sad. And if Saturn is unfortunate and does not aspect Jupiter, but aspects the Sun and Moon, he is born sad, with many anxieties, and <unclear>firod</unclear>, and tongue-tied, and a lord of the heart <note>possibly meaning he is ruled by his internal emotions</note>.

# On the Degrees of those born with failing sight

### On blindness of the left eye
Know that when Saturn and Mars increase in light and afflict the <term>Part of Fortune</term><note>A mathematical point in a birth chart representing well-being and luck.</note> or the lord of the light of the Moon when it is below the earth, or if the Part of Fortune or its lord is in the house of the thongs <note>original: "domo loris", likely referring to a specific astrological binding or constraint</note> and they afflict with blindness of the left eye. Others say that if the lord of the sign is the Sun, the one born will have a disease and be blind in one eye, and in the same way when the Sun is retrograde from an aspect, he is blind in one eye when the misfortune is not apparent; and when the Sun and Moon are with masculine planets and are not apparent, they are either [blind in both] eyes or, if there is blindness in one eye, the vision is clear in the other.

### On the Good and Fortunate Magistrate and on the work done by a clever and talented man.
And if the Sun is the significator <note>original: "aspicis," referring to the astrological aspect or planet signifying a specific life area</note> of the profession and is masculine and in a fixed sign, it adds to the fortunate nature of the fortune. If, however, it is in a movable sign, it will be less good. If it is in a common sign, it will be mediocre and elevated. If it is in its own place <note>its own zodiac sign</note> or in a contrary and malevolent sign, if it is like a master in its own sign, the native is elevated in his work. And if it is unfortunate in a strong and malevolent place in his work, if a fortune <note>a lucky planet like Jupiter or Venus</note> is placed there, he will be diligent and hold his place; but if a malevolent planet is placed as the master in its detriment, he will have pain in his work, death to his person, and great labor for the native. And if the significator has mercy, it is pleasing; it is called the significator in the house of its delight and kingdom, the native will not worry about his work and will rise in the kingdom and show himself fully in his work. And if the fortunes aspect it, he does work that joins and moves things; if the misfortunes aspect it, and especially if the native is at work in judgment and labor, it leads the native to abandon the work. But if Mars prevails over Jupiter in the height and exaltation of the profession and dominates the significator of his work, it will happen with loss and in his own affairs.

### On blacksmiths, goldsmiths, painters, and the like
And if it is in fire signs, the work will involve fire, such as a goldsmith, a baker, a cloth-maker, and the like. If it is in earth signs, the work will be of the earth, such as masons, diggers, woodworkers, lime-burners, and cleaners of mills and flour-makers. And if it is in air signs, there will be a battle of the air: these are messengers, trumpeters, jesters, and more. If it is in water signs, the work will be of water and soft things, such as fishermen, water-carriers, guides, and there will be sickle-users, cloth-washers, those who pull out fish, and the like.

### On the visible profession of the native
And when the sign in which the profession is located is "deformed" <note>referring to specific zodiac constellations considered 'mutilated' or 'imperfect' in form</note>, regarding the visible profession of the native: they will be blacksmiths or those who work with iron, and jesters, and it is seen in them as if they were made of iron and do not fear those beasts. And if it is another sign of human form, they will be painters or barbers, and all works will be for the persons of men. ->On the birth of a furrier, a maker of cloaks, and others<-

<margin>On the carpenter</margin>
If Jupiter <note>original: ♃</note> appears, and especially in a bestial sign <note>Signs representing animals, such as Aries, Taurus, Leo, etc.</note>, it signifies that the newborn will be a furrier. In conjunction with Saturn <note>original: ☌ ♄</note>, if Saturn appears, he will be a maker of cloaks and other items such as capes, garments, and threads. In conjunction with Jupiter, if Mercury <note>original: ☿</note> appears, he will be a worker of horn and wool. In conjunction with Mars <note>original: ♂</note>, if the Moon <note>original: ☽</note> appears, he will be a tailor and perhaps will make cloth for men. In conjunction with Jupiter, if the aforementioned does not appear, he will be a worker or smith of iron.
If the birth occurs when the Sun <note>original: ☉</note> is present and Mercury appears in the "house of masters," it can signify that the newborn will be right-handed <note>original: dextra</note> and signifies he will be a carpenter of spears, shields, wagons, <unclear>talomoz</unclear>, and wooden instruments. In conjunction with Saturn, if Saturn appears, it signifies he will be a carpenter of houses and of all things which endure, a builder of dwellings for the nobility. In conjunction with Jupiter, if Jupiter appears, he will be a master of saddles, shields, and great instruments. In conjunction with Mars, he himself or the aforementioned children [will be] kings <note>Likely a reference to high mastery of the craft</note>. In conjunction with Venus <note>original: ♀</note>, if Venus appears, the newborn will be a maker of certain smooth stone instruments and high things, and instruments held by the clergy in the Church, such as a bishop’s staff, and the like. In conjunction with the Moon, if the Moon appears, the newborn will be a manual laborer and a maker of instruments for bridges. In conjunction with Mercury, if the Sun is in one boundary and others are in a masculine sign—moving in Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius—the newborn will be a merchant of legumes and also a carpenter.

->On the birth of one who will be a tanner and shoemaker<-

If at birth Venus is finally present in any of the narrow conjunctions, and one of them is in a fiery kingdom and the other in a bestial sign, it signifies the newborn will be a tanner of clean hides and bridles. In conjunction with Saturn, if Saturn appears, and clean with Saturn, the newborn will be a <unclear>sarpitus</unclear> who cleans garments within walls and carries a cloak. In conjunction with Jupiter, if mixed with Jupiter, he will be a maker of bridles and <unclear>padosium</unclear> harnesses and those things pertaining to dress. In conjunction with Mars or Mercury, if they end with Mars, it signifies he will be a worker of <unclear>corgu</unclear> which are appropriated for houses and a cobbler of leather. In conjunction with the Moon, if it appears, he will be a tanner and a shoemaker of <unclear>ruigiorum</unclear>. In conjunction with Mercury, if Mercury and the Sun are finished, he will be a maker of reins and red leathers pertaining to the scabbards of swords.

->On the birth of one whose mastery will be sculpture or painting<-

If the newborn has Venus in the term of Mercury, and Venus appears in conjunction with the Moon in the middle of a sign, it signifies the newborn will be a scribe or painter. In conjunction with Saturn, if Venus appears with Saturn, it signifies he will be a painter of all colors. In conjunction with Jupiter, if Venus appears with Jupiter, it signifies he will be a maker in wood and work with rust and iron and things pertaining to leather straps. In conjunction with Mars, it signifies he will be a worker in bone. In conjunction with the Sun, if it is in the place of the Sun with Venus, it signifies he will be a painter of bronze and all precious things that have beauty. In conjunction with Mercury, if it is in the place of Mercury with Venus, he will be a writer of faithful letters, such as those who are in [holy] orders, and he will decorate with gems. In conjunction with the Moon, if it is in the place of the Moon, it signifies he will be a sculptor in clean [stone] or in red, or pertaining to water; and when in the house of Mercury and the Moon, the master [planet] touches him or is in the succeeding angles or appears extraordinary, it signifies the newborn will be subtle in the work of his hands. In conjunction with Saturn, it signifies all writings made in the building of houses, or of all things made of linen, or expensive ironwork and the molds for money <note>i.e., a die-cutter for coins</note>.

->On the birth of one who will be a dyer<-

If at birth Venus and Mars are in the center of the place of mastery and have a finished connection as it appears, it signifies the mastery of dyers, especially if it is in a watery and fiery sign. If Saturn appears, he will be a dyer of black cloths. If Jupiter appears, he will be a dyer of <unclear>paullorum</unclear> and trumpets. In conjunction with Mars, if Mars appears, it signifies he will be a dyer of red cloths and all things which have grayness, beauty, or light. In conjunction with Venus, if it is in the place of Venus with Saturn, he will be a dyer of the brightest things and all green things and those colored with medium colors and iron-colored things. In conjunction with the Moon, if it is in the place of the Moon with Mars, he will be a dyer of saffron and all things similar. In conjunction with Mercury, if it is in the place of Mercury with Mars, he will be a dyer of wool.

->On the birth of a miner of minerals<-

If at birth Mars and Saturn perform the work and it is in an earthly sign, the newborn will be a digger of the earth for iron. In conjunction with Saturn, if Saturn appears, he will be a digger of silver and precious stones. In conjunction with Jupiter, if Jupiter appears, it signifies he will be a digger of <unclear>naliuoz</unclear> and all things made for war and for the fear of demons. In conjunction with Mars, if Mars appears, he will be a digger of springs and lakes and dark, split crevices. In conjunction with the Sun, if it is in the Sun, it signifies he will be a digger of wells and soft places. In conjunction with Venus, if it is in the place of Venus, it signifies he will be a digger of <unclear>ozroz</unclear> and places through which they carry water to clean places. In conjunction with the Moon, if it is in the place of the Moon with Saturn, he will be a digger of <unclear>lamaz</unclear> and cloth.

->On the birth of one who has the mastery of navigation<-

If at birth Saturn and Jupiter are in the middle of the sky <note>The Midheaven or Medium Coeli</note>, the newborn will be a sailor or perhaps a master of ships. In conjunction with Saturn, if Saturn appears, the newborn will be a sailor on the sea according to the customs and all the <unclear>infertorum</unclear> which occur in kingdoms and rivers. In conjunction with Jupiter, if it is in the place of the Sun and Jupiter, he will be a sea sailor for the purpose of wars, and this when finished with Mars and when the Sun appears in conjunction with the Moon.

# On the Born Apothecary

If Jupiter ($\text{♃}$) or the Sun ($\odot$) and Venus ($\text{♀}$) are the lords of the work and there appears an aspect of another, he is a skilled apothecary and a seller of medicines. # Concerning the Birth of a King or the Lord of a Kingdom or City

If **Saturn** <note>original: $\hslash$</note> and **Jupiter** <note>original: $\jupiter$</note> are in **Mars** <note>original: $\mars$ (interpreted from 'maste')</note> in the **Midheaven** <note>The highest point in the sky at birth, indicating career and public life</note> and the **Sun** <note>original: $\odot$</note> is in **Trine** <note>An aspect of 120 degrees, considered very harmonious</note>, the newborn will be a King in the obedience of the devout, a lord given to his father and to counsel. He will be a man of good generation, from whence he is born; and when he is born under a bad sign, he will be diligent in his affairs, for his strength fears the Lord in his foundations. He shall be made free in his ample and great providence of provinces, joined to his own houses.

**Concerning the birth of the lord of any Kingdom or City**
If the **Ascendant** <note>The sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</note> appears with the **Sun** to the **Sun**, the newborn will be a lord of souls and kingdoms, far from hunger and dominion, given by providence. **Jupiter** in the **Ascendant** and in the **Midheaven** signifies a birth in a great and high place of order. When **Jupiter** and **Venus** <note>original: $\venus$</note> move that kingdom and dominion, it is great. **Jupiter** in the **Ascendant** adds to the middle and the line; and when there is fortune in the sign of **Saturn** in the **Ascendant**, or if **Venus** and **Jupiter** appear in the **Ascendant**, the birth is of great renown in command and cities, faithful in person and in his revenues.

And if the lord of the generation is the **Sun** near the tenth day, and the lord of the fullness is **Jupiter**, devoutly placed in the **Ascendant** up to the middle of that sign and in its **Augment** <note>A point of increased planetary strength</note>, the newborn will be of long fame and devotion among the greatest lords of lords, in dignities and mandates. They shall have friendship and happiness in the provinces; banners <note>original: vexilla</note> shall be raised for him and he shall fulfill the mandates of the people. When the **Sun** is in the **Oriental Angle** <note>The eastern quarter of the chart</note> and **Venus** does not appear in the **Ascendant**, and fortune is present, the newborn will be a great lord and will have praised dominion. In his dominion, he will be named for the memory of good divine action.

When **Jupiter** is in the **Ascendant** appearing with **Venus** and the **Sun**, and they are visible with **Jupiter** from the **Midheaven**, the newborn is a lord who will have command over others and fulfill every mandate. Unless the **Ascendant** is such that **Jupiter** is present in the **Ascendant** and in the **Midheaven**, the newborn is a lord of good form and good memory, and will have dominion from the king of his lordship, who trusts in him.

**Jupiter** in the **Ascendant** and the **Sun** in **Mars**, with **Venus** and **Jupiter** appearing in the house of the **Sun**, the newborn is a lord of praise, mercy, and titles, adorned with the mercy of his enemies; he shall be a man where praise is shown and spoken among his people. **Jupiter** in the **Ascendant** appearing with the **Sun** from the **Ascendant**, the newborn is a lord of fortunate birth. **Jupiter** in the **Ascendant** and in the **Midheaven** without the appearance of the lord of the [opposite] house, the newborn is a great and high one who commands others.

When **Jupiter** endures in his sign in the **Midheaven** in the nativities of lords, he will be fortunately strengthened from a great place, of a high order of lordship and kingdom and high mandate. When **Jupiter** is in the **Midheaven** and **Venus** appears in the **Ascendant**, the newborn is a judge and is judged by lords, and he shall reach the lords because he rules the fathers of the progeny.

**Concerning the newborn who will be a leader or commander**
A birth under **Jupiter** in the **Ascendant**, or with **Jupiter** when **Venus**, the **Sun**, and **Jupiter** appear from the **Ascendant**, the newborn is a Master of Soldiers <note>original: magister militum</note>. With **Jupiter** receiving the strength of others in the **Ascendant**, he is named a famous leader and father; that name shall be of noble origin. When **Jupiter** is in the **Ascendant** with **Venus**, and **Mars** is in the **Midheaven**, the newborn is of great power, a victor of victors.

When **Mars** is in his **Joy** <note>A specific zodiacal sign where a planet's influence is most natural</note>, he will be the head of soldiers before whom banners are carried; he will be a lord of wars and of great things. If **Jupiter** appears, he will be famous, renowned, and highly adorned. When the **Sun** is in the **Angle of the Earth** <note>The Fourth House or Imum Coeli</note> and **Jupiter** is in the **Midheaven**, the newborn is a Master of Soldiers, very subtle in showing victory to cities.

When **Saturn** and **Jupiter** appear from the **Ascendant**, he will be a lord of horses and a head of soldiers, a great and honored lord, especially in a **Masculine Sign**. When the **Sun** appears with **Jupiter** and **Venus** in a masculine sign, the newborn will be a renowned commander; they shall call him a moderator and ordainer of wars, and because of this, he shall conquer and have what he desires of the spoils.

When **Jupiter** is in the **Ascendant** and the lord of life, and the **Sun** and **Venus** are in his **Face** <note>A 10-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign</note>, especially in the habitations of lords, he will be among great men of long fame and power. Banners shall be for him, and he shall be a lord of wars and great things, a lord in iron and strength. When **Jupiter** and the **Sun** are in the **Ascendant** and appearing outside the rays [of the Sun], the newborn will be a great and powerful head of many soldiers, a victor in military matters. He shall not fear lords and shall exercise such providence. When the **Sun** is in the **Midheaven**, the newborn is a son of parents who is elevated under fame; he is a lord and a head of many kings, and when he invokes anything of his words, they are fulfilled. From the birth of the **Sun** and **Jupiter** with **Mars** in the **Midheaven**, the newborn will be of great name and praise, an ordainer of soldiers, carrying banners and invading fierce towns and castles.

### On the birth of the wealthy and on acquiring money

If any lord of the 2nd <note>The Second House in astrology governs personal wealth and possessions.</note> should be at the <unclear>maste</unclear> <note>Likely a scribal abbreviation for a specific planetary position or strength.</note> and should be with friends of a good life, and if **Jupiter** appears then at the end of his life, rays will appear to him. ### Concerning the native who is given gains, houses, vineyards, fields, and lands

<margin>1. 2. 12. [numerical references to houses or degrees]</margin>

If the ascendant or the Midheaven or the 10th [house] and the lords are running in the light, he inherits land, houses, and seed, and whatever he has, he has lordship and fame. If the Lord of the Fourth and Jupiter are bound together, he has profit and builds houses and buys vineyards and fields. # On the praise and assurance of one born to be a merchant

From a distinguished fiery aspect, when Saturn <note>original: ♄</note>, Jupiter <note>original: ♃</note>, and Mars <note>original: ♂</note> appear, and especially when Jupiter and the Sun <note>original: ☉</note> are in motion, if they have weak friends <note>referring to planetary "friendship" or favorable aspects</note>, the person remains good and honest for a long time. Jupiter is a sign of water, and from Jupiter himself, the native <note>the person born under this sign</note> receives great riches and trade. **On the native praised as a merchant.**
<margin>Jupiter with Venus <note>original: ♀</note>, Mercury <note>original: ☿</note>, and the Moon <note>original: ☽</note></margin>
When Jupiter, Mercury, and Venus appear with the Moon, and the Sun is present, the native is praised as a merchant. If Jupiter, Mercury, Venus, and the Moon are in the house of Jupiter and are strong, he will possess riches and make many trades. If Jupiter, Mercury, Venus, and the Moon are in a good place, the natives will gain riches as good merchants with wisdom and prudence. If Jupiter, Mercury, Venus, and the Moon are in a wretched aspect with Saturn and he rejoices, even in that place he will be a good to middling merchant; he will live throughout all his estates and will have friends among faithful kings. If Jupiter, Mercury, Venus, and the Moon are in the house of Saturn and perish, and the Sun and Mars are in the rays <note>combust or near the sun's glare</note>, and it is a nocturnal birth, the Sun will be near the mouth <note>perhaps a specific degree or house cusp</note>; the native will be disgraced and will suffer poverty. But if Jupiter, Mercury, Venus, and the Moon are in the middle of Saturn's influence and Jupiter appears, it is called a misfortune; yet from this, he will be a strong merchant, a buyer and seller of good fortune. If the native has Jupiter, Mercury, Venus, and the Moon in trade, but they are in the sign of Saturn and Jupiter does not appear strongly, and they fall into the water of fortunes <note>likely a reference to a "watery" house or sign</note>, the merchant is more likely to perish or be stingy. If Jupiter, Mercury, Venus, and the Moon are in the house of Saturn, he is a wealthy merchant and performs trade with thousands of gold items. If they are in the house of Saturn and he prevails in trade, the native of that sign will rejoice in trade and have fortune. If Jupiter, Mercury, Venus, and the Moon are in the greatness of Saturn, the native acts as a merchant and shows himself through knowledge and honor. If Jupiter, Mercury, Venus, and the Moon appear with the Sun and Mars, the native is fortunate in trade from the middle of his life until the end. **On the native of mediocre status in the world and the poor—that is, one who is neither rich nor poor.**
<margin>Saturn with Jupiter, Mars, the Sun, Venus, Mercury, and the Moon</margin>
When Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, the Sun, Venus, Mercury, and the Moon act as a misfortune, but fortune appears from a strong place and the Sun is strong, and Jupiter and Mercury are in their own aspect, the native lives in a mediocre way in the world and completes his life as such; his children will be like others. If Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, the Sun, Venus, Mercury, and the Moon are in the rays, he spends much; if they produce little in the water, he will be in his first state. If Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, the Sun, Venus, Mercury, and the Moon are unfortunate and follow one another, the native will be of a good sort and thus passes through life without perishing, a person of good life as he ordains his affairs. If Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, the Sun, Venus, Mercury, and the Moon are both appearing as misfortunes at the Sun's birth, the life is one of misfortune, as he says, and so he will give to the world. If Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, the Sun, Venus, Mercury, and the Moon are in a strong place and there are three aspects from the middle where Saturn is, with long fortune and misfortune, the native will be in vice, yet in the world he is not poor. If Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, the Sun, Venus, Mercury, and the Moon are in a wretched, evil misfortune at first, but Jupiter and the Sun appear strongly in aspect at the end, he will be strong in his actions and will rejoice; these are the sides of the native in his life. Between misfortune, friendship, and poverty, if Jupiter appears by the support of the good, then misfortunes and fortunes are in the teeth <note>perhaps "at odds" or "in the clutches"</note> of each other; the native will have both riches and poverty in the world. If it is said to perish in the aspect of Saturn in many nocturnal births, and Saturn appears in nocturnal births as a misfortune, then by Saturn's misfortune, the fortune is more often rich than poor. If Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, the Sun, Venus, Mercury, and the Moon are in a strong good place and Jupiter, Venus, and the Moon appear fortunate, but the aspect perishes through his own people, or if they are in a weak place, the native is of mediocre fortune in the world, with both riches and poverty.
<margin>On the wretched, poor, and hardworking native</margin>
<margin>Saturn with Jupiter, Mars, the Sun, Venus, Mercury, and the Moon in misfortune</margin>
When Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, the Sun, Venus, Mercury, and the Moon are in an aspect that is retrograde, as a combination that perishes, the native appears in misfortune; in an unfortunate place, he will have less and will labor. With Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, the Sun, Venus, Mercury, and the Moon in misfortune, he is a poor, sad man in his life and lives in poverty, forced by debts for a worthy cause. If the native has Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, the Sun, Venus, Mercury, and the Moon in an aspect of misfortune from the Sun or Moon, he is hardworking and labors with his body, compelled by debts and by a strong seal <note>perhaps a legal or fated obligation</note>, or he himself will think to have it. If Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, the Sun, Venus, Mercury, and the Moon are with the Moon in misfortune and Saturn or Mars is in aspect, it is said he produces something, but sometimes Jupiter does not appear; misfortune itself returns a profit upon him, but the native is hardworking and perishes in evil; he has laborious things in all his members so that he labors and finds that evil pleasing; and all the misfortune of the water <note>perhaps referring to the humors or a specific zodiac sign</note> is how he wishes to consume his life. If Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, the Sun, Venus, Mercury, and the Moon have the Moon in a good place, but Jupiter, Venus, and the Moon are in a place of misfortune, such as being without a home or hidden in a vile place, the native appears in misfortune; he is hardworking in evil and poverty, and as he perishes, he cannot be anything but poor. If Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, the Sun, Venus, Mercury, and the Moon are through the passions of death in aspect, and the Moon was fortunate but perishes in the end, the native is hardworking and of bad character in his days; he will have his life in labor and evil. If Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, the Sun, Venus, Mercury, and the Moon are in an evil place in the sign of an unfortunate Jupiter, and the native perishes by the Sun and Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, the Sun, Venus, Mercury, and the Moon, the native is hardworking and unjust; he will make friendships in his life. If Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, the Sun, Venus, Mercury, and the Moon are in aspect by a night birth in an evil place, he eats in poverty and friendship, unless God willed otherwise. **On the good native.**
<margin>Saturn with Jupiter, Mars, the Sun, Venus, Mercury, and the Moon in good standing</margin>
When Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, the Sun, Venus, Mercury, and the Moon are in their greater houses, the native will be worthy and it returns [the result] below...

# Concerning Servants and Captives

### Concerning brothers, sisters, and those born as strangers

And I know then that if there should be a malignant influence <note>original: "maligno," referring to a malefic planet like Saturn or Mars</note> in the place of the brother, it appears he shall be free, yet misfortunes are given by that man to another place; in this way he causes money to be destroyed and he persecutes. ### On the misfortunes of the native's brothers, and their downfall and evil death

# On the quantity of the children of the native

<margin>On the children of the native who are famous and honored</margin> Dorotheus <note>Dorotheus of Sidon, a 1st-century astrological poet</note> teaches two things in his fifth book: Look to the two lords, namely the Sun and Moon, in one sign; calculate from them to the Ascendant <note>The degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at birth</note>, and the number between them designates the quantity of children. And Alkindavor <note>Likely Al-Kindi, the 9th-century "Philosopher of the Arabs"</note> says: Look to the Part of Children <note>A mathematical point in a birth chart calculated by adding and subtracting the positions of specific planets</note> where it is and where its lord will be, and calculate from the place of the lord to the Part, and the number between them designates the quantity of children. And he says that you should look at the Part and look at the House of Children <note>The 5th House in a horoscope</note>, and if they are with the lords of the children, and what the distance is from the seventh year until the lord of the lords, and which of these will be aspecting the House of Children; and if in a masculine sign, it indicates masculine heads <note>sons</note>, and what will be in the person specifically and <unclear>properly</unclear> so. **On the lords of the children of the native:** He who finds two things—the lord in the Part of the Sun and something of the native in the Ascendant and in the House of Children—then he will be a man of children; as the Sun is to the Ascendant, then they shall increase. Otherwise, they will be few, as he may see in every Part of Children toward the fifth house or the Ascendant or the twelfth house.

# On the goodness, fortune, and joy of the native from children

And recognize if it appears in the nativity of the lord of the native that he <unclear>desires</unclear> that the native shall rejoice in his children and shall have them in his strength and goodness. ### Concerning the children of the native who are hardworking, foolish, and fearful, and the better among them

<margin>Concerning children of the native who are entirely bad</margin>
In their place, it is then similarly deformed and a lifter of the world <note>likely referring to a specific planetary elevation</note>. If indeed Jupiter and Mars were in these signs, they will have thoughts and things which they do not want, and cares. Concerning the bad death of the children of the native, and the few deaths of the children, and those who shall die.

<margin>Concerning the children who shall remain</margin>

->**On the Evil Death of the Newborn**<-

Or if Jupiter ♃ and Venus ♀ are in the angles <note>The 'angles' are the four most powerful points in a horoscope: the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli.</note> and in a malevolent sign at the mid-point of time, and Mars ♂ or the newborn are connected to beasts; if Jupiter ♃ is in a malevolent square and the Sun ☉ is in the Midheaven and Saturn ♄ is in the seventh house, it is assigned that they shall be eaten by beasts. **On the death of the newborn by decapitation and by execution.**
<margin>Saturn ♄</margin> And when the Lord of the House of Life is in a malevolent 1st or 7th house from the aspect, and the Sun ☉ is the Lord of the 1st, the newborn's fate is deferred; the Sun ☉ and Saturn ♄ from the aspect and Jupiter ♃ in the 1st, and if by chance he does not aspect him, the newborn will be killed by thieves <note>original: "latronibus"</note> such as a highwayman. **¶** Likewise, if the Lord of the 1st and the Lord of the Sun ☉ are in the 8th house <note>The 8th house is traditionally the House of Death.</note> in affliction, and Saturn ♄ is in a religious sign with afflictions that impede the conjunction, the newborn will be killed in a royal prison; and when one of the afflictions is in the Midheaven and is very great, the newborn will be killed by hanging. **¶** Likewise, if the Sun ☉ is in an eclipsed malevolent aspect and Saturn ♄ is in the seventh, the newborn will be killed by predators or by kidnapping.
**¶** Likewise, when Saturn ♄ is in the Midheaven, the newborn is detained, and if Saturn ♄ is in opposition and aspects him with force from the angles and does not bind itself with it, that newborn will be killed by thieves just like a man. **¶** Likewise, when Saturn ♄ is in the 10th sign of the Sun ☉ from the aspect, and with Jupiter ♃ or Venus ♀, if the newborn is killed without fault with a rope, and perhaps with pain and hanging. **¶** Likewise, when Saturn ♄ with Mars ♂ from the aspect and Saturn ♄ is in the height and aspects the 10th from Saturn ♄ in detention, he will be killed and gibbeted <note>To be 'gibbeted' was to be hung in a cage or chains as a public warning.</note>. **¶** Likewise, if Saturn ♄ is in conjunction with the Sun ☉ and the Lord of the 1st is in a malevolent place, the newborn will be killed by the sword. **¶** Likewise, if Saturn ♄, Mars ♂, Jupiter ♃, and Venus ♀ are in aspect, the newborn will be killed in an evil hour while fighting. **¶** Likewise, if Saturn ♄ and Mars ♂ are "dead" <note>A planet is 'dead' or 'peregrine' when it has no essential dignity in its current position.</note> as in a single earth, the newborn will be killed and gibbeted. **¶** Likewise, if Saturn ♄ is in the 8th house of the newborn, the newborn dies a rigid death. **¶** If Saturn ♄ is impeded by Mars ♂, likewise by iron. **On the death of the newborn who shall be suffocated by his own hands.**
