# On the good journey of the native
<margin>On the good journey</margin>

...full, if it joins with the testimony of the <term>planets</term><note>The wandering stars used in medieval astrology to determine fate.</note> and thus it is said regarding the journey, those seeing in that full state the cause of his [the native's] movement toward some <unclear>ascension</unclear> and all the <unclear>prognostics</unclear> and thereafter both fortune and preservation. **On the good journey**
<margin>On the good journey</margin>
**H**ere it is said that when it shall be in the aspect of a strong fortune <note>A "fortune" refers to a benefic planet like Jupiter or Venus.</note> and he has not had testimonies with him regarding the <unclear>journey</unclear> for the native, he shall rejoice in that <unclear>manner</unclear> and shall achieve his goals; he shall be known and worthy of much love and he shall <unclear>return</unclear>.
**I**f, however, it is in the <unclear>zodiac</unclear> by aspect, and when the aspect occurs, it indicates the native will love journeys and seek them out; he shall have profit from joy. And if it be in the house of <unclear>Venus</unclear> and the <unclear>Tail</unclear> and <unclear>Head</unclear> <note>The Dragon's Head and Tail, or Lunar Nodes.</note> appear, it signifies for the native joy and profit, and he shall make many journeys; when it is strong in him, the native abounds in travel and shall do good things, so that he sees no journey without joy and sees much that he loves, though <unclear>adversities</unclear> may come.
**I**f, however, it is toward the better good by aspect, and when the months are in the house or any better state, he wishes to have profit; if it has been <unclear>distant</unclear> from the <unclear>roots</unclear> <note>The "radix" or natal chart positions.</note> of the person and does not appear. **B**ut if it be in <unclear>Sagittarius</unclear> and <unclear>Capricorn</unclear> when by aspect the native finds a <unclear>journey</unclear>, he shall have much profit. **I**f, however, it is in a <unclear>sign</unclear>, namely from the name to the sign of the name, the native shall make journeys and from other fortune shall find much profit and honor.
**I**f, however, it shall be in the house of Venus, the native will love journeys and rejoice in them by great counsel; by the greatest counsel if it shall be strong in the house, and the native rejoices in his journey and shall see good and honor. **I**f, however, it was by aspect and the lord <note>The ruling planet of that specific house or sign.</note> shall be in aspect, the native will love journeys and rejoice in them and be swift in going. **I**f, however, it be at some time or perhaps on the day of <unclear>Venus</unclear> for the native, and that fortune was oriental <note>Rising before the sun.</note>, it indicates all things toward a fortunate journey; it shall be in its own house and they see strength from themselves in their journey, and it shall appear. It [the chart] unfortunates him, for it speaks of long journeys and going for months from place to place. **I**f, however, it is with great strength from misfortune, it leads him to it, for he shall be on a journey and shall have his face toward the hour of <unclear>Venus</unclear> and shall not cease from them until death. **On the journey of the native of which he himself [is part]**
<margin>On the journey of the native of which he himself [is part]</margin>
**I**f indeed it is from that which shall be in the place where the native had a son on a journey, it shall come to pass wickedly. **I**f indeed it does not come, recognize it from the middle of it and the rays in which the native had his right hand, and it comes especially to him. **I**f indeed it be in the house where the native shall always be, it concerns many things for his business. **On the journey from which the native shall come by misfortune**
<margin>On the journey from which the native shall come by misfortune</margin>
**O**r if it shall be in his own house, the native shall have a long journey if his own comes to him. **I**f indeed it be in aspect and he had some part in the house of the journey where the native has a long journey, if it comes to him. **I**f indeed it be in aspect and where it is and the aspect shall be, the native sees many journeys and they shall come. **I**f, however, it be in the manner where the native sees many journeys and they shall come.
**On the unfortunate, bad, and painful journey of the native**
<margin>On the unfortunate, bad, and painful journey of the native</margin>
**I**f indeed the unfortunate [planet] shall be in its own house and its lord is unfortunate and in a bad place, let the native have bad losses on the journey and it shall not be well. **I**f, however, it be in the signs and from them, and misfortunes appear from the months, the native shall be of a bad journey in a cursed time and shall have his punishment and many evils. **I**f, however, it be in aspect and he himself appears to wish it, the native will go on many journeys and in them he shall <unclear>complain</unclear> much; and a burden from the aspect on the native from the day of the native toward much journeying and pain. **I**f, however, there be an aspect toward him in the house of the journey, the native has pains and labors on the journey, neither profit of honor nor anything that will please him. **I**f, however, there be an aspect from <unclear>Sagittarius</unclear> in the native regarding evils, he shall have bad journeys and soon has evils. **I**f, however, it be in the house where the native was in those journeys and had losses, he seeks a better profit. **I**f, however, it be on a journey of his own, they see the native shall have bad journeys and shall be of evil. **I**f, however, in these two teachings you recognize the sign of misfortunes, if the native be by sea, he has many evils in his hand on his journey. **I**f, however, the lord of one be in aspect, and aspect in aspect, and it shall be in aspect and misfortunes do not appear, the native has miserable bad journeys and the native approaches himself. **I**f indeed the lord himself gave it and it shall be falling from aspect by night, it shall not appear; it will hinder the native with misfortune and in labor and evil on his journey from himself and they see it. **I**f indeed it joins the full testimony of a full journey from a bad place in time, the journey of the native is very bad and there is labor on the journey. **I**f indeed the lord be to the lord by himself, he shall be unfortunate in the sign; recognize that the greater part of the native's journey in aspect shall be more strongly bad, with labor and sorrow. If, however, he recognizes misfortunes because those misfortunes are by themselves, it shall be evil, and the journey draws from robbery and wars. **I**f, however, it was in the sign of the moon, the greater part of the journey is by the moons <note>Perhaps meaning months or lunar cycles.</note> through the forest and deserted places. **I**f, however, the lord of the aspect shall be going to the lord of the journey, the native in whatever journey the lord shall be in, comes to the lord of the aspect and shall follow his journey with tribulation and hardship.

### Concerning the fear of whether a matter turns out well or not
Then if there shall be a malignant <term>aspect</term> <note>original: "aspextus"; the geometric relationship between planets</note>, it will be bad whether the thing is good or not, because it is corrupted by the name of the hour and the pledge of opinion itself; in a word, the man is in <unclear>doubt</unclear> if the <term>aspect</term> in the man is evil.

### Concerning a person being born
Then if it concerns a person who is being born, whether they ought to live or not: calculate the name of the child and the mother, and the name of the day on which they are born—namely the day of the month—and add 301 and divide by 9. And if one remains and it is odd, they shall live; if it is even, they shall die. <note>This describes a form of onomancy, or divination by names and numbers, common in medieval medical astrology.</note>

### The Part of Rain
Let it be taken by subtracting one motion of the Moon from the Sun, and let what remains be placed from the Moon in the 3rd place, and they truly add to the 3rd place; and where the number is limited, there is the "Part of Rain" <note>A specific mathematical point in a chart used to predict weather</note> in that sign and degree to be judged.

## Revelation of those things which are in the waters
And if it comes to those houses which are "the asses," then the Sun or Moon shall precede in the middle.

### Concerning the Opening of the Gates
Whether for rains, winds, heat, or cold, any of these is then found when a <term>planet</term> was ready to receive that thing. Look to the Moon: if you find her separating herself from Saturn and applying to the Sun, or separating from the Sun and applying to Saturn, it is the "Opening of the Gate" of Saturn. If you find her separated from Jupiter and applying to Venus, or separating from Venus and applying to Jupiter, then it is the "Opening of the Gate" of Jupiter. If you find her applying to Jupiter in the hours of the Sun, whether it be open or not, it shall be the Sun's opening of the gates. Look to Jupiter and Saturn; if they are malignant in the gates of the same, then when the Sun is in <term>aspect</term>, they see this.
<margin>wind</margin> It is wind if in the matter of rain or heat or cold you find the Moon in a humid sign applying to a humid <term>planet</term>; thus let the opening of the gates be, and have confidence in rain.
If you find greater things from the opening of the gates, pay attention as it seems to God concerning the air, and when the Moon was with the Sun in one minute. And pay attention when the Sun is in Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius, Pisces at 180 and 190 and 227, in 210, in 217, in 328; and then provide how it may be. And when it is applied another time in an aspect which is judged, pay attention to something from the aspect of the gates and judge according to its nature how the Sun or <term>planet</term> is opened. Then leave the aspect if you find them applied or in aspect to one another; the <term>instator</term> <note>likely a corruption of "instigator" or "indicator"</note> of things collected or received is then for the Moon to take the names without the nature of <term>catatui</term> <note>unclear technical term, possibly a corruption of a Greek or Arabic astrological term</note>. From nothing itself, it is as I [judged] rain, then for cold, cold; for heat, heat; for winds, wind; and too much snow confirms it. Or as when the Moon in Venus and Mercury are <term>oriental</term> <note>rising before the sun</note> and <term>retrograde</term> <note>appearing to move backward</note> or of slow motion; and if any of the <term>planets</term>, or two of the higher ones, withdraw or are of slow motion, there will be rain without doubt.
In the Sun 20, the conjunction of Saturn travels through each year; the stars of the east will strengthen and certify in their places. You should diligently attend to whether the Moon and Sun apply, as well as Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, and Mercury; <term>occidental</term> <note>setting after the sun</note> planets touch upon sudden rains in the first of every hour without end.

### On the discovery of the ascending degree

<margin>
If you wish to find the ascending degree of any birth
</margin>

Since you wish to find the ascending degree of any birth, first consider the degree of the Sun <note>original: $\unicode{x2609}$</note> and the Moon <note>original: $\unicode{x263D}$</note> as they preceded the birth. If the Moon preceded the birth, it is "pre-conal" <note>referring to the syzygy or lunar phase before birth</note>; if the Sun, then it is "conjunctional." Consider the degree of the degrees in which the conjunction is found and look for the *Almuten* <term>Almuten: The planet with the most dignity or "power" over a specific point in the zodiac based on five essential criteria.</term> over it—namely, the strongest in that degree through the five testimonies. Observe those signs at the hour of birth according to the Almuten, whether it be above the earth or below the earth. For if it was above the birth through the upper part of the horoscope, it is not valid; then the ascent will be through the Almuten. Therefore, when the birth of a child is found and we wish to find the quantity of life, we seek the **Hyleg** in such a manner: first, it is considered whether the birth was by day or by night. # The Treatise of William of Vrane on the Use of the Astrolabe

<margin>The path of astrological prediction</margin>
It is pleasing to those who disparage out of ignorance, or rather for the sake of envy—those in Germany who, whatever they do, study more to criticize others—that for your sake and for the honor of other students desiring to know the truth, I hand down to posterity this memorial of myself, as has been done so often among the ancients. ### The Book of Haly explains that concerning the planets under the rays

<margin>Saturn</margin>

# On the Appearance and Nature of Men

¶ And a man full of flesh and of a fleshy build with a beautiful face has large eyes; he possesses fullness because of his beautiful face. ## On the Moon in Scorpio

**Scorpio** governs the groin, the testicles, the anus, the bladder, the womb, the menses, and the marrow, as well as their infirmities, great difficulties, hemorrhoids, and the flow of blood from the eyes, cataracts, and dimness of vision. When the Moon is in **Scorpio**, a fixed, northern, dry, and watery sign <note>original: "hẏdico"</note> of flux and phlegm, I do not see that it is good to begin anything, for then the Moon is in her fall and misfortune. It is not good to bleed the median vein at this time. Likewise, do not undertake travels, nor climb trees or mountains; indeed, do not wonder that the median vein is not to be bled then, so that the wife may perform her duties <note>original: "vt vxor dā faciat"</note> according to the aforementioned warnings when this sign rises in the East.

## On the Moon in Sagittarius

**Sagittarius** governs the thighs and spots on the face, and the narrowings that are in the limbs, as well as the fingers and other members, and their infirmities such as rheums and impediments. It signifies heat and the burning of others, and impediments from falling and the danger of lingering limb pains without a clear cause. When the Moon is in this southern, hot, and dry sign—choleric and masculine—it is good to be joined among friends, to settle disputes, and to let blood. It is good to arrange a memorial if it does not stand in the way, for it is not a time for a wife. It is good to enter a bath, to begin a journey toward the East, to proceed with a trading journey, and to do all things involving fire. It is good to prepare rooms and to do all things pertaining to fire. It is bad to work on things pertaining to dysentery, or to perform plantings, agriculture, or medical treatment of the hips while the common lords of the aforementioned things rise in this sign from the East. The weather is hot and dry.

## On the Moon in Capricorn

**Capricorn** governs the knees and their inner parts and their infirmities. When the Moon is in **Capricorn**, a southern, tropical, dry, and earthy sign of cold and phlegm, it is good to sow grain and plant vineyards, and to do all things that are of the earth and for the earth. It is good to begin a journey toward the South and to set out for trade, and to do all things that must be completed quickly. It is bad at this time to begin a journey toward the North, to take a wife, or to do anything that must last a long time. It is bad to build or to dry things out, to engage in intercourse, or to do anything involving fire. It is not good to let blood, nor is it advisable to take a wife. Medical treatment of the knees or for flux is not advised. The weather is dry and windy, and it scours the earth and the world through the air without water, and often there is fog.

## On the Moon in Aquarius

**Aquarius** governs from the legs down to the lower ankles and heels, their inner parts, and their infirmities, such as the contraction of the limbs or what the common people call "emania" <note>Likely a corruption of 'mania' or a specific regional term for a nervous affliction.</note>, feverish black bile, or pains of the veins. When the Moon is in **Aquarius**, a fixed, western, hot, and moist sign—airy, sanguine, and masculine—it is good to build a house, to take a wife, to enter a home, to let blood, and to do all things that do not need to last forever. It is bad to treat the legs or to undertake a long journey. Do not do things that require speed or winter conditions. The weather is calm and watery. It is good when leaving port and for all the common things mentioned above as this sign rises from the East.

## On the Moon in Pisces

**Pisces** governs the feet and their extremities, their inner parts, and the infirmities and pains of the feet. When the Moon is in **Pisces**, a northern, cold, and watery sign of flux and phlegm, it is good to take a wife, to cross over for friendships, to handle money and silver, and to do all things pertaining to water, such as water mills or aqueducts. It is good to begin a journey, especially toward the North. It is good to take a wife and to do things that promote growth. It is bad to treat the feet or any of their parts, or to do anything involving fire. The weather is watery and cold.

## On the Signs and the World

The **Tropical Signs** are these: **Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn**. When the Moon is in them, the weather is changeable, for at the entry of the Moon into these signs, the weather changes according to their nature. Each sign has its own space and influence over the world, invading and presiding over its own domain.

Fixed or firm and stable signs are <term>Signs</term> <note>original: "Signor."</note> and all 320 of the horizon; they are called "fixed" because when the Sun enters their beginning, their form does not change in its essence. Rather, they are hot, and even if they are firm, they remain so despite the imbalance of watery or dry air, which is clearly seen in them according to the seasons of spring, summer, autumn, and winter.

### On the Natures and Manners of the Planets

Since we wished to proceed briefly regarding these degrees of heaven, we are now ready to write a few things about the order and natures of the seven planets. There are seven planets which are called "wandering stars" because they move through the zodiac in the sphere of the fixed stars. Almighty God placed them above this starry heaven so that they might move beyond it to regulate the impulses of the firmament. <term>Saturn</term> <note>The furthest and slowest planet in the medieval cosmos, associated with melancholy and old age.</note> possesses by nature the breadth of the circle of signs between these and the stars. The Sun itself causes the midpoint and, like a fountain of light and heat, illuminates and warms all things arranged above, opposite, and below it, creating the diversity of long periods such as years, months, and days. If anyone acts according to the hours of the planets below, etc., because when a planet is malevolent, it desires evil things in its will, even though its essence is said to be in its own dominion. When they are in their <unclear>house</unclear>, they cause many evils and diseases, especially when in the first house. In that <unclear>house</unclear>, there are wonderful supports for moving implacable hatreds. From this planet, in the first month of conception, its coldness chills the conceptus in the mother, curdling and drying it. And because he desires eyes and faces of a blackish hue, Saturn ♄ creates few hairs in the beard and <unclear>locks</unclear>; he casts his eyes down toward the ground as he walks, has lean eyes, yellowish skin, and poisonous veins. He is harmful in his time, yet clever in anger, with a sharp face toward people. He is accustomed to breaking stones, destroying houses, building, and closing; he possesses craftiness, saying one thing with his mouth while plotting another in his heart—concerning Saturn.

<margin>The power of Saturn</margin>

The second planet is Jupiter ♃, who is above; Jupiter is benevolent and lovable, hot and moist in nature. He favors all good things and harms no one. If he is in his own houses—in Sagittarius ♐ in the first house and Pisces ♓—Jupiter is greatly benevolent, especially in his timing, and lifts minds toward conception. He gives form and limbs to the conceptus. He makes his days beautiful, sharp, and light; as the law writes, they are numbered. Then people wash themselves in beautiful cloths, as is seen, and those who appear in serene colors are seen in such colors and similar things. He makes men human, ruddy, of beautiful stature, and of good character. They are trustworthy, they are leaders, having large and broad front teeth, long hair, and a full beard. In those days, they are merciful, loving the good and detesting the evil—concerning Jupiter.

Mars ♂ is the planet below Jupiter, and he is much feared and very malevolent. If he is in his own houses, Aries ♈ and Scorpio ♏, he works much discord, war, snares, and evil ways. For in his malice, he desires to diminish the appetite for good through the excessive nature of the soul; therefore, the goodness of a man diminishes the appetite for evil and increases the appetite for good. As it is said, the appetite for evil is often hindered by the other. Mars ♂, in his months of conception, composes the bones and internal parts of the conceptus. Regarding colors, although they are mostly red, they are partly brown, as is often seen. They confirm sins, dishonor, and move wars and strife between friends. They are of the fire-bearers, such as blacksmiths, butchers, cruel shedders of blood, and those who deal in burnings and taking vengeance—concerning Mars.

The Sun ☉, as it is said, is the fountain of light and heat and the light of the world, providing the diversity of human seasons. Furthermore, the Sun ☉, placed below, illuminates all things, and they are hot and dry. When it is in its house, Leo ♌, it moves very intensely and its heat is great, and then the days are pleasant. The Sun ☉, in the fourth month of conception, gives the conceptus the heat of the blood, the heart, and the liver.

## On the nature of the fixed signs

The firm or **fixed signs** <note>original: "signa firma vel fixa"</note> are four: namely Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius. They are called firm, fixed, or stable because when the sun enters the middle of them, it is literally fixed in its being and does not change. If it was hot, it will be so [continually]. For example, if it was intemperate, it will remain intemperate, and so you may know of other things like clear weather and similar conditions. It is clearly seen what the minds are like, as in summer, autumn, and winter, in the fourfold time of their own stability. In these firm, fixed, or stable signs, things standing in them are continuous at all times. It will be good, and I say good, for whatever one pleases to build, to obtain, or to celebrate, whereas the aforementioned movable signs betray. If you wish to act against a wife <note>or "for a wife"</note> so that she might return to her husband, she does not return further to him. Likewise, concerning leaving prison: if one was in peace and death or among friends, they will not succeed unless many remedies are applied, for the devastation will not be quickly mitigated. And if it was a vineyard or [crops], it will prolong its [growth]. Therefore, accept the beginnings and divisions; it is good. While the sun is in them, it is good to leave prison; otherwise, it is bad for all things. It is good because the master cannot further offend him by imprisonment. While in these signs, it is [risky] to put on or make new clothes, especially if they are hindered; if one intends to profit from it and act and pray, he intends to move. The fixed signs are permanent for the works of masters which we intend for the altar and the battles of kings. Because Leo is fixed, they give in that sign a multitude of victories over all evil.

## On the nature of the common signs

The **common signs** <note>original: "signa communia"; also known as mutable signs</note> or "double-bodied" <note>original: "bipista" / "bicorporea"</note> are namely Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces. They are so called because when the sun reaches the middle of them, the time is mixed; its first half is hot and the other cold, or the first is cold and the following hot. Because in that time and [condition], a middle quality of nature is assumed. Their first half follows the preceding sign, and the second part assumes the following powers. In these signs of the body, if one buys something, it does not remain long with the buyer. If anyone is born in these, he will be considered fraudulent and a flatterer. And because their works differ, see that in them friends should not be trusted; if friendship is strengthened, it falls into decay and instability, and often causes divorces. Benefits given and received profit very little. Let him beware lightly lest he thinks a matter is firm and stable. In things begun in these signs, if someone moves from a house, they will move again within not many days. Whether for triumph or good or evil, in a double sign, it is now apprehended more fully.

In Aries, one is more subtle and [lean], and in man, it possesses abundance and gives a man wide, reddish hair, a sweet and large belly, thick legs, and a tall stature.

### Concerning the triplicity of the airy nature
A certain triplicity results from air, namely Gemini ♊, Libra ♎, and Aquarius ♒. It is called "airy" because they are of the air, and it produces windy men and bitterness at the first and higher levels. Regarding the air, just as they have limbs, they govern the arms and the hand. This nature grants a tall stature, neither small nor slight, and a large, distinct, and honest personality; it is faithful and constant in spirit. Libra ♎ possesses beauty and grace; it governs the internal organs and gives a decorative face, moderate flesh, and makes people lovers among their own kind; likewise, women are loved by men. Aquarius ♒ individuals are distinct; they sell their reasons <note>perhaps "arguments" or "judgments"</note> and are proud. However, they are sublime and of honest reason. They are bold according to all their goods, and in whatever way or on whatever day they allow themselves to be deprived, they are favorable and overflowing; they have one thick vein, unlike others of the triplicity of the aquatic nature.

### Concerning the triplicity of the aquatic nature
A certain triplicity results which is aquatic, because these are humid places. Everything that comes from humidity is water, and all things that exist through water and a multitude of water. These are, among others, the principal children of humanity. For example, Cancer ♋, regarding the limbs of men, possesses the chest and the breast. They have a very thick body, thick in the front according to the upper half, slender below and thick in the middle. It also gives crooked teeth and small eyes. It <note>the triplicity</note> possesses all the female vessels and testicles <note>likely referring to reproductive organs generally</note> and makes its subjects lean and thin when they fight, with a round face, and narrow, small, and numerous eyes. Pisces ♓ possesses the feet and makes its subjects' bodies large, bold, voracious, and high-spirited; they are prone to greed and temptations. They are better in the breadth of purgatives <note>medical treatments intended to cleanse the body</note> and are [unclear] and give better feet.

### Concerning the quality of the first triplicity
Secondly, the first triplicity consists of Aries ♈, Leo ♌, and Sagittarius ♐. It is oriental (Eastern), fiery, and of a choleric <note>the "hot and dry" humor associated with anger and energy</note> cause, and thus masculine. Inasmuch as the month acts through which fire is generated, they are of humidity and supreme heat in their generation. Leo, Sagittarius, and Aries belong to the day; they are Eastern and they grow hot.

### Concerning the quality of the second triplicity
The second triplicity consists of Taurus ♉, Virgo ♍, and Capricorn ♑. It is meridional (Southern), cold and dry, melancholic <note>the "cold and dry" humor associated with earth and introspection</note>, earthy, and feminine. They are fleeting and [unclear]; Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn belong to the day; they are Southern and lack heat.

### Concerning the quality of the third triplicity
The third triplicity consists of Gemini ♊, Libra ♎, and Aquarius ♒. It is of an occidental (Western) cause and is considered sanguine <note>the "hot and moist" humor associated with blood and a cheerful disposition</note> and masculine, therefore warm and humid. Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius belong to the day; they are all powerful in heat, they [unclear], and they become moist.

### Concerning the quality of the fourth triplicity
The fourth and final triplicity consists of Cancer ♋, Scorpio ♏, and Pisces ♓. It is septentrional (Northern), cold and humid, aquatic, and feminine; and because of the humidity, it is called feminine. Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces belong to the day; they are Northern and are called humid. | Here it ends.

As Albumasar <note>original: "Albumasar"; referring to Abu Ma'shar, a famous 9th-century Persian astrologer</note> says in the introductory volume which he composed concerning the judgments of the signs and planets, I intend to explain something regarding elections <note>The practice of choosing the most auspicious time to begin an action</note> so that those wandering from the path of truth do not neglect to read the books and waters of physics <note>Natural philosophy or medicine</note>. This is so they are not held back by ignorance, which leads to filth and dryness. He knows well how others have been led into error by malice; wishing to show these things clearly and to reveal the way of truth to the faithful, he established this book. He compiled it from the sayings and experiments of all the ancient wise men, and it was tested many times through great labor and study. He left it arranged by tables so that those things written in it might be found more easily, and so that one might find in it the significance of each day regarding good and evil, and what should be done or avoided in all business.

I have published in this book what I think should be said more clearly regarding the days, showing which sign looks toward which planet to see if there is any space on Earth, and whether the aspect is "dexter" (right) or "sinister" (left).

A <term>Sinister</term> aspect is when it looks at one in front of it at a distance of 60 degrees. An <term>Opposition</term> <term>Sextile</term> <note>The scribe likely means the relationship between aspects here</note> is when it looks at a planet behind it at 90 degrees—though a <term>Sinister</term> <term>Square</term> aspect is truly when it looks at a planet behind it at 90 degrees, or in front of it when a planet is in the same degree and minute of a sign. Or where each planet is distant from another by 180 degrees and 6 signs <note>This defines the Opposition</note>. And a <term>Trine</term> is according to more and more <unclear>degrees</unclear>. 

One should act according to the will of the aspects of the planets, seeing whether it be <term>Conjunction</term>, <term>Sextile</term>, <term>Square</term>, <term>Trine</term>, or <term>Opposition</term>, as was said above. Afterward, look at the name of the table and the city where you wish to be, the sign of the aspect, and the name of the sign in which it resides. If two planets appear, one good and the other evil, that day shall be "middling" in all works. If three planets appear and two signify good while one signifies evil, proceed with the work. But if two planets signify evil and only one signifies good, let the person beware.

<meta>This page continues the astrological "elections" (choosing the most auspicious times for specific actions) based on the position of the Moon in the zodiac signs, attributed to the Persian astronomer Albumasar (Abu Ma'shar).</meta>

# The Elections of the Days

<note>original: "Electiones diei" — the practice of choosing the best time to start an activity based on the stars.</note>

**The Lord of the Day** <note>The "d. l." likely refers to the "Dominus Diei" or Lord of the Day, the planetary ruler.</note> is good for building foundations and houses and everything lasting and ancient. **The Night** <note>ny. d. for "noctis die"</note> is good for vacations and rest, and for reading books. **Jupiter's Day** <note>♃ d.</note> is for generating delights and joys. **Mars' Day** <note>♂ d.</note> is good for drinking curative medicine with the help of a physician and for rest. **The Sun's Day** <note>☉ d.</note> is good for baths, cutting hair, and being adorned. **Venus' Day** <note>♀ d.</note> one will delight in wives and daughters, and it is good for the entry of a beautiful girl. **Mercury's Day** <note>☿ d.</note> is good for building foundations and everything lasting and firm. **The Moon's Day** <note>☽ d.</note> one will delight and rest; it is good for entering baths.

### Elections of the day when the Moon is in the first part of Aries <note>♈</note>
The Moon is for generating rest and vacations from all work. For the whole day, washing, rejoicing, and rest are good; it is good to enter baths. **Jupiter's Day** is limited; it is good to use baths and rest and to treat of good morals. **Mars' Day** is vile; it is good to enter baths and cut hair. **The Night** is good to enter baths, rest, and be delighted. **The Sun's Day** is also vile; it is good to enter baths, rest, and be delighted. **The Lord of the Day** <note>ong. d. l. — possibly "ongoing" or a specific planetary hour</note> is good to use the fingers <note>perhaps for massage or manual arts</note>, to wash, and to be adorned at the highest time. **Venus' Day** is for rest and vacations from all works; it is good to enter baths. **Mercury's Day** is for rest and vacations from all works and for rejoicing. **The Moon's Day**, **Jupiter's**, and **the Sun's** are good for entering baths and resting.

### Elections of the day when the Moon is in the "Galia" <note>possibly a corruption of 'cauda' (tail) or a specific lunar mansion</note> under the rays of Taurus <note>♉</note> and Aries <note>♈</note>
On this day, in all works, it is not very good to go before kings nor to ask anything of them. **Jupiter's Day** will be loved; it is good to enter into secrets and finalize something. **The Lord of the Day** is good for treating secrets and abstaining from service and approaching them. **The Sun's Day** is to be feared in all things; it is not good to walk upon the sea, nor to take medicine, nor to paint. **Venus' Day** is great; it is not good to engage in trade, nor to become pregnant, nor to reveal anything. **The Night** is hateful in all things; it is not good to make a partnership, nor to celebrate weddings, nor other works. **Mercury's Day** in all things and for merchants and commerce is nothing except in secret and hidden matters. **The Lord of the Day** is amiable; it is good to enter baths and be adorned with ornaments and to use means. **The Moon's Day** is great; it is not good to buy victims <note>sacrificial animals</note>, nor to drink, nor to send announcements. **Jupiter's Day** is not good for taking a god <note>perhaps an image or oath</note>, nor clothes, nor servants, nor to take a journey, nor to make a visitation. **The Sun's Day** is amiable; it is good to take all things before the battle and to dig wells. **Mercury's Day** is great; it is not good to walk upon the waters, nor to enter the bath, nor to drink medicine.

### Elections of the day when the Moon is in rest and the rays of Gemini <note>♊</note>
**Aries' Day** <note>or Mars</note> is to be feared; it is not good to borrow, nor to move, nor to wear your clothes, nor to act. **Jupiter's Day** is [vatū?]; it is good to make wives ready and to disclose hidden things. **Mars' Day** is good for making a trade pact, receiving a dismissal, and dealing in spices. **The Sun's Day** is vile; it is good to enter the waters, to treat with captives, and to intercede. **The Night** is vile; it is good to treat with captives and merchants and those who are in hiding and wild places. **Venus' Day** is good for entering among writers, selling secrets, and extracting hidden things. **Mercury's Day** is vile; it is good to be delighted and adorned and to treat of captivity and binding. **The Lord of the Day** is good for treating of one's own affairs and extracting secrets and hidden things. **Jupiter's Day** is good for entering the market and receiving and treating with captives. **Venus' Day** and **the Moon** in their own [velun̄?] and they rest with their wives.

->And so is the end of Albumazar on the Elections of the Days<-

These images work in love and hate for those who know well the course of the planets.

I, Albert the German <note>original: "Albertus Teutonicus", referring to Albertus Magnus, the 13th-century scholar and saint often associated with alchemy and magic</note>, of great surname, loving and preserving chastity, searching and discussing with study **Concerning the second marvelous seal of properties**, having scrutinized the ancient philosophers, found certain books of some most natural men regarding their judgment in the science of the stars. They said that he <note>the practitioner</note> would produce effects in the tables of the stars and the aforementioned worlds, though with great distinction of constellations as I have found elsewhere. Neither in the books of the saints nor in sacred writings is there such a notable seal, for it has a marvelous power. Examining some of my own powers, I tested it and found it most expert. 

Therefore, see what I have described and noted: namely, on the day when the Sun enters the sign of Aries, if it be in the fourth house or in that house full of light, or if it be in the ascendant or justly placed, then let such an image of the first day be made. And it shall be in the sight of God as in other books which have treated these things. From this Aries <note>the Ram</note>, let it be carved or impressed in iron with black writing, or in purest gold. And know that it remains in the sphere, and these are its virtues which I have seen, namely:

**First**, that when they carry it over the heart, they gather a marvel to themselves and it removes the passions of the heart. **Second**, if anyone falling from the falling sickness <note><term>falling sickness: epilepsy</term></note> carries it upon themselves and drinks wine in which it has been placed for a day of fasting, they shall be freed. **Third**, if anyone suffers pains of the veins or belly or the stone <note>kidney or bladder stones</note>, and carries it tied near the loins, they shall be freed. And we have proven this many times: that squill, ambrosia, and bittersweet in wine often act against the stone in the bladder and make one pass the stone upward <note>likely meaning out of the body</note>. And similarly, squill thus bound to the thighs with ambrosia will drive away the pain of the heart and the stone. **Fourth**, against poisonous beasts: no beast shall strike him as if with venom. And if you place it in water and he drinks of that wine on a fasting stomach for nine days, he shall be healthy from the same, and such things as are in the soul and in the belly and in other members. Moreover, let it then heal in that wine and water such things as an abscess <note>original: "apostema"</note>, being rubbed in the water, and let him wash with it externally. And if such water be sprinkled in the house near the corners <note>original: "culos", likely corners or openings</note>, nothing shall kill him, such as serpents. **Fifth**, [for a woman in labor] let her place the seal at her thigh... then she shall give birth without danger. **Sixth**, it alienates [evil] from her. **Seventh**, such a leader shall be able to bear it and return wherever he wishes, nor shall he be able to be defeated; from then on he shall be victorious among soldiers like a lion among animals. **Eighth**, it is such that in a seal of filigree and preservation and works of incantation and sorcery, it puts demons to flight and dissolves all things. This has been proven many times because those bewitched by the charms they were given come to him, and if the master be present, they would give them the danger in wine given to drink, and they recover wonderfully. **Tenth**, if anyone on that day carries it over the heart, hatred and all envy in him is dead and understood as such; and no plea comes to him from anywhere to speak, especially to nobles and powerful men, for he binds them with justice. And when he sees it, he shall lose his talkativeness and [look them] in the face, and they then shall give him jewels and many such things. If he wants something from any prince or prelate, let him hold the seal in judgment or in his hand firmly. **Finally**, it is such that it increases goods, and for children it is placed, and for the conception of a woman, etc.

# The First Judge, Belbor, on Life

1 Blessed be God who has granted that you shall be long-lived.
2 You shall not rejoice in offspring, for fortune is currently turning against you.
3 Your enemy shall perish, and the wise man shall live for a long time.
4 Regarding the illness, it is said that he shall thus escape it quickly. <note>original: "evasurus cito"</note>
5 He goes securely, and as a companion, he is clearly healthy and safe.
6 May the highest piety provide for you in that which you are doing.
7 A favorable fortune happens to you, pleasant enough.
8 In that which you now seek, it seems you will have little profit.
9 Well, well, he thrives and sends a sword to you; he holds it. <note>This may be a metaphorical warning about a gift or a literal reference to a weapon.</note>

11 Stolen goods shall be returned to you; the thieves shall die by hanging. <note>original: "morte suspensa"</note>

16 Abandon this lawsuit you desire, lest you have sin.

### Here Begins the Letter of Isaac Albedanus to Seleucus, King of the Persians

<margin>7</margin>
<margin>6</margin>
<margin>4</margin>
<margin>8</margin>
<margin>9</margin>

To Seleucus, King of the Persians, Isaac Albedanus sends greetings. You seek the paths <note>original: "lamos," likely a corruption of "lemos" or "vias"</note> rather; greetings to all, for I have found nothing that releases one from cares if at the same time the play of a prince has persuaded you through envy to resist. Your most true secrets, which proceed in turn, will marvel at me more; the devoted have implored them. You desire to know how to apply yourself to study so that you can then, as much in the distant present as afterward, address the question of the signs of the places <note>astrological houses</note> and the lots <term>sortes: a method of divination, often geomantic or numerological, used to determine outcomes</term> of the body, following the books of the ancients. If you question the few faithful things which I afterward announced to you and the public, namely in the work of *Zedech* <note>likely referring to Jupiter, "Tzedek" in Hebrew, or a specific astronomical treatise</note>, it is called a great labor. This science of the *Gomes* <note>possibly "Gomer" or a technical term for geomantic points</note>—the distance of the Signs arranged in the place of the heaven—was first accepted by the ancients of the world as recognized; scarcely one will rightly attempt it. With the highest study and twin vigils, I have finally opened it as labor compels, by your illustrious command. 

But to negotiate concerning this one thing: within twelve hours, you shall make the lines of the four primary ways formed in turn, one of the primaries being unknown; you change them through the twelve called [houses], to which the remainder will be made. Refer to those things assigned by the lots. The Indices <term>Indices: in geomancy, these are specific figures that "point" to the final outcome or "Judge"</term> likewise, where they are sent to the question in this manner: namely, in the first of the voices, the remainder in its own theme, and the Indices which my line finds at the extreme; and such will happen in the year. Finally, as the Judgment <note>original: "Indicium"</note> which can be known even from the holy findings, yet with the primaries accepted; for if any third, then the first, then the end through one or the second or the third. If they should be on one day in their own theme, which you lead, then in the same names you will find the Indices by counsel in their place, just as I have marked in writing to me the primaries of all things. Nor can this seem to be an assent for you, that the Indices of the two witnesses should be openly doubtful; we have attended to this according to the present business, more than is necessary here, so they may be distinct. And those questions which can most be known are the domiciles <note>astrological houses</note>, in the manner in which this business is to be conducted. 

The first doctrine in the present work brings forth and explains the hours, with this added: that the shoemaker <note>likely a metaphorical term for the practitioner or a corruption of "sector"</note> may introduce the places of the signs distinguished by their names, which the wise man of heaven introduces and shows. They call these the *bassenas* <note>unclear technical term</note>. Through this, not a few things are added which are to be done, and by frequent mission to an equal consolation, it defines such doubtful things for the greedy and the [pious]. Although it is not right for me that these things be traded in such a small way, it shows not grace but excessive [skill], and they praise that it is arranged by modes and art alone in a lesser faith. One must not be deceived, but **Follow** the full teachings of Albedanus sent in this work concerning his questions, which he induces to be done many times; and he speaks of the signs to be truly understood, which can scarcely or never fail.

### These Spheres pertain to the aforementioned Isaac Albedanus

If a purchase should proceed: from A to Capricorn, it is praiseworthy; if from A to Sagittarius [it is otherwise].
Concerning memory: if to Capricorn, it is better; and worse to *Beth*; if of the whale to *Biah*. <note>These appear to be phonetic renderings of Hebrew letters or Arabic geomantic terms used as coordinates.</note>
If a fugitive: he will return if to *Cap lanch*; if to *Sacty*, he will go to *Salaan*.
A man will obtain a woman: if to *Qd pset* under *Napich*; from *Napich* to *Nasman*.
If he sends concerning that which is sought: to *Qd d)* *Salma* is *Alma*; to *Amlaa*; from *Amlaa* to *Ssaat*.

̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄̄ # Ladan. 27.a

<margin>28</margin> Pray to God that prosperous things be sent, provided you change your ways.
<margin>24</margin> Without a master, let him prepare to depart; fortune wishes it to be done for her.
<margin>26</margin> You desire what you see, but it remains stuck; yet, friend, have faith.
<margin>27</margin> You do not desire all things, if you become a pauper in all things.
<margin>28</margin> Use this garment; thus you shall always live honorably.
<margin>23</margin> This work consumes itself; you understand this to be the point.
<margin>22</margin> Though it may come slowly, yet redemption itself shall happen.
<margin>21</margin> Do not desire this woman as a wife, lest you find a better one <note>The Latin implies a warning against settling for a current choice when a better match may exist.</note>.
<margin>20</margin> Confine yourself to your own; for the enemy's troop is harmful.
<margin>19</margin> You desire future things which are not destined to end for you.
<margin>18</margin> Let this not go to the youth; what you take up, he seeks to destroy.
<margin>1a</margin> Suddenly, friend, fortune shall send ruin upon you.
<margin>16</margin> In an unfortunate way, the highest point has just been born for you.
<margin>17</margin> Thus safe with a judge, your rights are pushed back into themselves.
<margin>12</margin> The dreams seen by you wish for good things before the ages.
<margin>13</margin> For whom the <term>prug</term> <note>original: "prug"; likely a corruption of "pyra" (pyre) or a specific gaming term</note> stands, you love, and you should remove the fault.
<margin>12</margin> To conquer thus truly would be the same as to seize.
<margin>11</margin> He loves this woman ardently, if she becomes a wandering flood.
<margin>10</margin> You shall not go according to the rite; after this, you shall return from there.
<margin>9</margin> <margin>fates</margin> The fates wish it so; many evils will come upon you.
<margin>8</margin> Thus returning pleasantly, it lingers for only a few.
<margin>4</margin> Those who gave the fates to themselves with a new weariness.
<margin>6</margin> Let lost things be restored, if they are held for a short time.
<margin>4</margin> The aforementioned things shall joyfully and decently restore themselves.
<margin>x</margin> It is better to command joy than to enter into that place.
<margin>3</margin> Just as it is sent, so saying to you, it is a bad life.
<margin>2</margin> If you remain upright within the walls, the enemy claims these such things.
<margin>1</margin> Seek what he seeks, whatever it may be, even by night.

# At Gadara .26.⁹
<note>original: "Ladarae"; likely referring to Gadara, a famous center of oracles and learning in antiquity.</note>

<margin>28</margin> Put aside this honor being given, lest it be taken from you <unclear>cruelly</unclear>.
<margin>21</margin> Whatever is adopted, know that this has been brought about by your deeds.
<margin>26</margin> Fortune gives these riches to those who have increased their <term>small means<note>original: "niculatis," likely a corruption of "funiculatis" or referring to modest beginnings</note></term>.
<margin>27</margin> May you conquer your enemies, or rather, may you conquer the one who is raging.
<margin>22</margin> Do not wage wars, nor should you seek to become a victor just now.
<margin>23</margin> Peace is ordained for you, but it is held under a specific condition.
<margin>22</margin> Let this be taken from you; then a good fortune is prepared.
<margin>21</margin> Believe that the effort is being made, yet it does not work out prosperously for you.
<margin>20</margin> You hope for those things to be given which can be denied by right.
<margin>19</margin> If you give to the Lord <unclear>in vain</unclear>, you will give a lasting gift.
<margin>18</margin> Divine power changes all things, even fortune.
<margin>14</margin> Regarding the children you seek, it will turn out poorly if they are denied.
<margin>16</margin> That which is seen by you should not owe you condemnation.
<margin>11</margin> I reveal to you that the dreams you have seen are not the last.
<margin>12</margin> After the business matters have been traded by your hands with labor.
<margin>13</margin> Neither in this case of theft, nor in anything else, will there be <unclear>reason</unclear>.
<margin>12</margin> There is a place where he may be led, so that a friend may be held as one to be loved.
<margin>11</margin> As quickly as you strive, you shall enjoy the things to be possessed.
<margin>10</margin> Let this be driven out quickly, and let it be held away from all.
<margin>9</margin> Behold, it is seen; joy is seen with the giver of profit.
<margin>8</margin> Here the woe is healed, and it threatens those who are joyful with love.
<margin>a</margin> He who endures lost things is not one who refuses to be harmed.
<margin>6</margin> The debts which are given are those which ought to be moved.
<margin>7</margin> May you be secure, even if the one to come is fearful.
<margin>2</margin> Your death is indeed of this kind, so that you may enjoy life as one born.
<margin>3</margin> This labor is not fit; it reveals when it is <unclear>perpetual</unclear> to you.
<margin>2</margin> For many, the <term>grace of labor<note>original: "labore gram" (gratia)</note></term> is unable; this is the teaching of the poor.
<margin>1</margin> Here he is well changed, who is prepared under our journey.

->Agalsar .2a.<-
<note>original: "Agalsar"; likely a rubric or name associated with a specific astrological or divinatory table.</note>

<margin>28</margin> This desire of mine hastens to take its step
<margin>24</margin> Honors are bestowed and multiplied
<margin>26</margin> Garments are condemned, nor are they then rejected by any

<margin>25</margin> Then, as if having pitied the head, he shall redeem him
<margin>23</margin> This friend of mine desires to have you as a spouse
<margin>22</margin> Envy has entered the tribe, yet it is prepared for you
<margin>21</margin> Renounce now those evil things of yours which are present
<margin>20</margin> May God be within you through your heavenly gains
<margin>19</margin> Bad fortune ceases, for soon blessed things are to come
<margin>18</margin> It is wise that you were born always blessed
<margin>14</margin> You shall stand joyful, for you triumph over the lowly <note>original: "per planta"; literally "by the sole of the foot," implying treading upon pride or enemies.</note>
<margin>16</margin> Ask the Lord, and let not all things be pleasing to you
<margin>17</margin> Do not make trades; the fates strike while they lead you
<margin>15</margin> This thief awakens so that he may steal hidden thefts
<margin>13</margin> For do not believe a malignant friend to be worthy
<margin>12</margin> Only now discerning, God himself is to be your companion
<margin>11</margin> Believe this virtue to be worthy and exceedingly kind
<margin>10</margin> He grants that they be just, and then you shall come to the end
<margin>9</margin> Better is the state which was then sorrowful
<margin>8</margin> When your people are in fault, your merit shall resist
<margin>4</margin> You live in the Lord; you are a debtor to them and do not repay those <note>Refers to spiritual or social obligations.</note>
<margin>6</margin> There is no fear in trembling; strength seizes you and remains
<margin>7</margin> Your life is heavy; death shall come to you as something sweet
<margin>5</margin> This work speaks; it speaks well of all pregnant things <note>original: "p̄gnenta"; likely referring to outcomes or perhaps literally to pregnancy/fertility.</note>
<margin>3</margin> If doctrines come, then you yourself should take the first ones
<margin>2</margin> Lest your things be lost, do not therefore be warned <note>original: "per monastur"; likely a corruption of "permonestur".</note>
<margin>1</margin> The seat is changed, nor are the gains of honor acquired

# Algalganam. 28. <note>original: "Algalganam"; likely referring to a specific geomantic figure or house in a divinatory system.</note>

<margin>28</margin>
All things of the earth go as they are aptly brought by the stars.
<margin>29</margin>
Witnesses know well how to set out the truth regarding garments.
<margin>26</margin>
You will not be a true victor if by chance you join in war.
<margin>27</margin>
The lineage rejoices, for the child shall be made free from <unclear>prison</unclear>.
<margin>25</margin>
Take this woman as your wife, for faith denies a better one.
<margin>23</margin>
No blame is given to you, for the enemy is overcome by your hand.
<margin>22</margin>
I tell you this: that which is hoped for is prepared by the Giver. <note>The "Giver" likely refers to God or Fate.</note>
<margin>21</margin>
Loss is presented to you; profit is not restored.
<margin>20</margin>
Fortune is yours; by the Giver, there is one hope and one salvation.
<margin>19</margin>
It is said a daughter is born, but she is not your greatest light.
<margin>18</margin>
Through this, the plain is conquered, and certain things remain.
<margin>14</margin>
The presence is sent again when it is noted.
<margin>16</margin>
The purchase of <unclear>colors</unclear> is made for the kingdom without labor.
<margin>17</margin>
The thief perishes in his work if he refuses to return the stolen goods.
<margin>15</margin>
In this sale, your friend will not desert you.
<margin>13</margin>
Let this way be crooked; it is better if you choose to stay.
<margin>12</margin>
This is a truthful equality and a sweet friend.
<margin>11</margin>
The traveler who returns is far enough away. <note>term: <term>peregrinus</term> (pilgrim or traveler); often used in geomancy to describe a planet or person in a foreign place.</note>
<margin>10</margin>
Divine virtue shall be given to you through medicine.
<margin>9</margin>
That which was lost is never called back to itself.
<margin>8</margin>
If you believe wrongly, you must still return certain debts to the Giver.
<margin>A</margin>
Nothing harms or hurts; all fear recedes from you.
<margin>6</margin>
Life remains for you, which provides twin joys.
<margin>7</margin>
The enemy and fire will lay waste to this work and this king.
<margin>5</margin>
Through doctrine, the talkative man is given; heavenly things are denied.
<margin>3</margin>
If you think these things are true, then do not change yourself in any way.
<margin>2</margin>
This honor is given to the leader; soon he suffers to depart from here.
<margin>1</margin>
This desired thing is given by the Giver, if it be pleasing to you.

# Hippocrates’ Treatise on Astronomy Regarding Medical Crises

The wise Ptolemy <note>Claudius Ptolemy, the famous 2nd-century astronomer/astrologer</note>, the most skilled of all physicians, says: He who is ignorant of this book <gloss>book</gloss> of astronomy, no one should commit themselves into his hands; for without this, the reasoning of medicine is blind and weak. Indeed, he who does not know this should rightly be considered a fool, so that he might seem more noble to himself than a lion. And he who truly understands will not arrive at the first or second movement except by my grace; otherwise, failure will occur due to ignorance of this art. Then, regarding the sufferings of a person, it truly seems that they are intertwined, lest he know nothing else. Furthermore, the physician-astrologer understands himself through all these things. It is worthy, therefore, especially for a man to treat an illness so that his work may reach its goal. A physician who does not perceive the law of the stars in the judgment of medicines will be ignorant of the nature of this light of healing books, even if he possesses great virtue and does nothing harmful in all his medicines. For it must be known that at the same time, at least when death approaches, the illness is seen; but he ought to know how it behaves as a friend of medicine, and he should observe the full water <note>likely referring to the tides or bodily humors</note>, for then the blood increases in man and in all animals; then the sea of nations <note>original: "mare de gentibus," possibly a corruption of "tides of the ocean"</note> is present, and then the swelling of their waves is seen to increase visibly.

### Concerning the Moon in Aries

Now let us see, for when the Moon is in Aries <note>♈︎</note> in the first line, an illness then occurs. And if it is in Aries, or in Libra <note>♎︎</note>, or in Capricorn <note>♑︎</note>, or Cancer <note>♋︎</note>, then the illness is caught because of excessive heat, and the pulse of the head will ache. He reasons within himself but the heat does not cease; the patient will be out of his mind and can scarcely speak. Sometimes he will suffer too much heat to the point of pain; the pulse will be very vehement. Then, blood should be let from the vein of the heart <note>a specific bloodletting site</note>, but it must only be done partially because of the heat and impurity. This illness should peak on the second day, and if it does not, then death follows within 20 days from that day. There are 3 degrees in Aries through which this appears, and more than this. And if the Moon increases in its light in Aries, or is in Aries and Libra in a fortunate aspect, it appears so. And then if it is in Libra, the illness in the head leads from there to the stomach, and it becomes inflated and burns; then the illness diminishes from him, namely for the one who cannot otherwise escape it. And if it is in Libra, then it is in decrease just as it is in Aries. And if the Moon is in Cancer or Capricorn, then damage and danger appear; when it appears there, the illness finds its end in evil; if it appears strong, death follows; if not, he will improve. And then the Moon leaves those aspects of which we spoke because of the Moon's motion and finds Jupiter <note>♃</note> or Venus <note>♀</note> here and there; then the illness comes to a "combustion" <note>a dangerous astrological state</note> upon him until death is massed together; and from that you will find nothing but death, unless he then improves. This illness is from white bile <note>term: white bile (fel album), one of the bodily humors associated with specific temperaments</note>. In each individual sign there are illnesses if the Moon is increasing in its light. And if the Moon or the Sun <note>☉</note> is in Aries, then there is illness in the head and he will go mad; it is born from phlegm in the head and white bile, with which there is blood from the nostrils and mouth. It will resolve by itself from the head without medicine, provided it is entirely gone. And if it is in Aries, he either dies or escapes, but not without great danger. Then the Moon proceeds into Taurus <note>♉︎</note>; then do not do business, but if the Moon was not aspecting Saturn <note>♄</note>, then he will die. In Taurus and in Libra, if the Moon is there with Jupiter or Venus, he will have illness in the teeth, and the Sun in Aries in winter will afflict him. His work appears so that he should give him medicine and a gentle amount of the water he desires, since it is water; and place him in a seat in a suitable place for a bath, and let him sit quietly, and let it be done while he sleeps quietly. And give him river water to eat <note>likely "to drink" or "consume with food"</note> what he wants, because there is no preparation for him, nor does he have need of medicine then, if it appears thus.

### Concerning the Moon in Taurus

When an illness occurs with the Moon in Taurus in everything, and the Sun aggravates it from Saturn or Jupiter, that illness is of the blood. Heat will be produced and it will be as if there is pain in the night; he cannot sleep and has a desire to drink wine. Truly, immediately with this, let blood be diminished; then he shall give medicine and it will return with stool and humor. And if it was in that Aries or in Taurus, it comes to him and harms him greatly; death perhaps at 10 days, since the illness is in the head. And if the Moon is increasing in its light in Taurus and Libra, it appears so; and the Sun is in Taurus and the Moon comes to Saturn or Mars <note>♂</note>, the illness is through bile, and then...
