### I was asked to make manifest the counsels of the philosophers
<margin>R</margin>egarding many questions, I was asked to make manifest the counsels of the philosophers concerning the superior impressions <note>The "impressions" refer to the influence of celestial bodies on the Earth's atmosphere.</note> and concerning good air and terrible air, and the causes of frequent flooding, heat, and cold, because the sciences of judgments <note>astrological predictions</note> and their compilations have been distanced from them—the sciences which they established, namely from their astronomers—and they have departed from the way of wisdom into the way of mere belief regarding these sciences. And for one wishing to contemplate the sayings of the philosophers, I shall divide this book into eight chapters: The first, on the common accidents of the planets and fixed stars and the impressions in the upper air. # Concerning several playful experiments, as well as true ones

First: If you wish to have writing on any part of the body that is invisible, and when you wish to make it black by drawing your finger over it, it will immediately appear very black. Work thus: Take <term>Vormaz</term> <note>original: "Vormaz"; likely a local or corrupted term for a pigment or earth like vermilion or a specific mineral earth</note>, an earth with which you may write whatever you please on the hand or foot. Let it dry on that part. You can indeed walk about among people; look as you please, or try it in any way. Then, put a piece of <term>charcoal</term> <note>original: "carbone"</note> in your hand and with it blacken the invisible writing arranged there, rubbing strongly. Then, as if by a blackened finger, it will immediately appear in a very black form, which is wonderful.

Second: If you wish to have invisible writing on paper or <term>parchment</term> <note>original: "cartha"</note> which, by applying fire and heating it from a distance, becomes black and visible. Work thus: Take the juice of an onion <note>original: "cepe succum"</note> and the juice pressed from it, likewise <term>Vormaz</term> and rock salt <note>original: "sal gemme"</note> mixed with water. Let the mixture be purified. Write as much as you want on white paper, and the writing will become invisible. When you wish to have it visible, apply it to a good fire and heat it strongly; immediately it emerges visibly, which is a very great miracle. You can also do this same thing with simple onion juice, and it yields the same result, but then—because it is among the odorless things—the simple juice (unlike the mixture) smells like an onion from the roasting; this experiment will then become known.

Third: If you wish to have writing that is invisible by day but visible at night, so that it appears invisible by day but visible and shimmering at night. Take <term>oak wood</term> <note>original: "Lignum quercum"</note> that is rotted and glowing at night <note>A reference to "foxfire," a natural bioluminescence caused by fungi on decaying wood</note>. This should be tempered with milk into drops; rub it and write with this mixture on the wall of a chamber or house. In a marvelous way, what is invisible by day will shine at night. Or otherwise and better: Take one part of rotten oak wood that glows at night, grind it, then temper it somewhat in the milk of a virgin woman, and write whatever pleases you; and so it shall be done formally.

Fourth: For gilding or silvering coins, such as those made of copper or anything similar. Take <term>quicksilver</term> <note>original: "argentum vivum"; mercury</note>, then smear it in a fine common powder and mix it thoroughly. If there is any <term>sal ammoniac</term> <note>original: "armoniaca"; ammonium chloride, used as a flux in soldering and metalwork</note>, shake it so that it appears clearly. Put a little of this ointment in your hand and rub it diligently; then rub the coin with it, and it will appear silvery or gilded. This is to be revealed to no fool! Under this <term>Region</term> <note>original: "Clima"</note> of deceptions, these experiments exist for <term>sophisticating</term> <note>original: "sophisticandum"; in this context, to "sophisticate" means to adulterate or create a deceptive imitation, often of precious metals</note>; because they are poorly made, they vanish and lose their appearance through fire. I have known many such <term>sophistications</term> by name.

Fifth: So that a groat <note>original: "grossum"; a silver coin</note> appears gilded. Rub it yourself with <term>sulfur</term> or with <term>sulfur</term> and <term>sal ammoniac</term>. Apply it to a linen cloth and rub the groat in it; immediately it will become reddish. To erase this same thing, use salt, and it will become as it was at first.

# The Book of the Fifth Essence

### Regarding the consideration of all transmutable things. In the name of Jesus Christ, for the service of philosophy and the gospels of God, for me in Christ and for the poor.

Here begins the book of the fifth essence <note>The "Fifth Essence" or "Quintessence" refers to a celestial substance, distinct from the four earthly elements, believed by alchemists to be capable of curing all diseases and prolonging life.</note> regarding the consideration of all transmutable things. In the name of Jesus Christ, for the service of philosophy and the gospels of God, for me in Christ and for the poor.

As Solomon says in Wisdom 7: "God gave me the knowledge of those things that are, so that I might know the disposition of the world and the virtues of the elements; the beginning, the end, and the middle of times; the vicissitudes of changes and the alterations of the seasons; the course of the year and the dispositions of the stars; the natures of animals and the rages of wild beasts; the force of the winds and the thoughts of men; the differences of shrubs and the virtues of roots; and whatever things are hidden and unforeseen, I have learned, for Wisdom, the artisan of all things, taught me." <note>original: "Deus dedit michi sciam horum..." This is a direct quote from the Vulgate Bible, Wisdom of Solomon 7:17-21.</note> This Solomon, the most proven of all in wisdom, spoke as one who had experienced these things himself. Therefore, fear the infallible God because of the shortness of life, and despise all dangers, because Solomon says in the same book: "They have come to the friendship of God because of wisdom and teaching." They make their vows, and we apply our whole body to this service. And he concludes the brief title of the book: The consideration of the fifth essence regarding all things, first investigated by me for more than ten years in the greatest misery of the Order of Friars Minor <note>The "Order of Friars Minor" refers to the Franciscans. The author identifies as a member of this order living in poverty or hardship.</note> according to the holy theologians and many others. Worthily written for the order of Jesus in the place where I remained with you, held in chains and affliction. And that sacred reading is worthy of praise, as much in the writings of physics as in the sacred laws; so it is possible, as we ourselves have seen. We have seen many dangers and other things to be seen by my own hands; I truly waited and sent to many other parts throughout the universe, so that what was in me might be sent to all, that my work might reach you. For I saw the truth in this work in such a way, with divine providence illuminating it in whatever region, even from my birth. Because he was here in this manner, by the mercy of God he grants the knowledge of the method, as I revealed a few years ago to those who already knew—namely the poor and the weak—and thus to those notable for their wretched and infirm rules. By the grace of divine goodness, they were healed by the most illustrious gifts <note>original: "deis," likely a scribal error or abbreviation for "donis" (gifts).</note> which I revealed amidst many bitter dangers, just as science and charity investigate for the whole common people. I rule in this book first to find the method through art, because God created nature for the hands of the needy.

**Section One**

It is necessary first that we know how things stand in the inconveniences of old age, by which in ancient times the impediments to a good life were found, and how life is lost in old age and in the elderly; and you shall live through dreams <note>The Latin "vives per somnum" is obscure; it may refer to a state of rest or a visionary state.</note> if God brings me to the right hand in all of nature which is this.

This is what the ancients labored for: to seek a remedy against the burning <note>term: adustion (adustio) — in medieval medicine, an overheating or "scorching" of the bodily humors, often associated with melancholy or aging.</note> of man, or rather, that which is entirely corrupted might be preserved from corruption. This is what nature contains and moves as a desire. Rasis the philosopher <note>Rasis refers to Al-Razi (c. 865–925), a Persian polymath and physician highly influential in medieval European alchemy and medicine.</note> says for certain that this is so. For while we are in the habitation of the body, we groan and are burdened by corrupted matter, or rather by our own instability. The prophet says of me: "Alas, what is in me!" And if I knew how to prolong life so much, it would have been fantastic and vain for me to seek a thing that is as perennial within me as the heavens are at the limit of corruption. For Rasis says it happens in this way by God's will: because the worlds exist through corruptions (which are the elements), nothing is generated from the elements except a work that can by no means reach the secrets.

**The Investigation of Our Heaven**

One must seek a thing that stands in relation to our body just as the stillness and the influence which is the heaven is in itself. Thus our "heaven" <note>In alchemy, "our heaven" often refers to the Quintessence or the perfected Elixir, which acts upon the human body like the celestial spheres act upon the world.</note> is that in which the whole body is said to be in truth with the four elements of the elements. Because heaven in itself is a simple and incorruptible matter, not receiving passions or impressions, nor are the things of God within it; so one must seek a thing that is neither hot like fire, nor moist, nor cold like water. Nor is it hot like fire (for then it would flow away from us) nor dry like earth, but it is something by grace, like the "heavenly matter of philosophy," in whose nature many other things are present—some hot, some cold—and it enters into you so that it may overcome with the highest miracles, so that it can replenish the nature of our body; and that is what God ordained for my life. And the philosopher says that there were highly exalted men who experienced this consideration, generated as much from artifice as from the wonders of kings, princes, and physicians.

It is called "burning water" <note>original: *aqua ardens*</note>, "divine wine," <term>spirit</term> <note>The volatile essence or "breath" of a substance.</note>, and "water of life" <note>original: *aqua vite*, or brandy/distilled alcohol.</note>. <margin>Note this notable point.</margin>

For there is one gold which is collected from the earth's mineral, not from lead, because "alchemical gold" which descends from a certain corruption is not the kind loved by the <term>philosophers</term> <note>The alchemists.</note>. But because it is the "son of the sun," it is then said that by the influence of the sun in the bowels [of the earth], and by the sun alone influencing it, this is incorruptible—not always, but by comparison. Therefore, that which is of a hot nature is the sun in its adornments; but just as the sun preserves heaven, so the four [elements] flow into us. I tell you, in the power of the generation of heaven—and this is more related—lest the spirit in our mind be said to discern itself in generation, and renewal is found.

<margin>In this chapter he teaches concerning the influence of the stars regarding the generation of things and their influence upon the world.</margin>

All things, as Solomon witnesses—because a city is a sufficient thing—cannot be known by the efficacy of speech alone. For example, paralysis is cured from the head, from the neck, from the chest, and in other members below; and others from the navel down and not from the upper region of the members. And that this happens is difficult [to understand], but then [consider] Galen's measure in the first [book] of *On Simple Medicine*: that the thing is to be sought in that which they have from heaven. And keep this in mind: that in the stars and the images of heaven, a thing is received and created with such great love that it is confused [with the celestial], so that heaven does not hinder it through the months in the constellations, for the virtues lie within them. And from those virtues, they flow from above to the places of love in the whole chosen earth; and things coinciding in the confused and pure earth... these were for these kinds of stars just as for another. He does not say this without doubt: this is a grace, just as through the Diamond <note>original: *Adamas*</note> below; and in the end, by the impression of some star, it is created in the earth, and from then on it possesses the influence and properties of the star. And so it tends toward the end constituted for it by nature, and toward that from which it [comes], as if from the water of the moon; or just as without sight it moves the sea to flow and rise, and then it receives the command to descend to the world. This the moon certainly shows to the stone through the moon, and not only then.

When the physician searches in the *penasse* <note>possibly a corruption of "pennas," feathers/fins, or a specific vessel</note> because of the name "burning water," it is said that no physician, physicist, or doctor knows this: that burning water is everywhere in water. Through this, we have our water to be made; then, as if entering the distillation in smoke, it is necessary that one part be in a single hole at the top, so that what is made is placed therein. The water mixes itself in the holes at the summit and ascends, which is called the "work ascending," and it distills below to the vessel through a channel in two parts; then it replaces it so that the thing may ascend perfectly day and night. This water falls into that which comes to the eye by its own will among the four. And the sending of the operation in this is that the burning water may become better; it is accepted that its operation is more for the removal of evils, it helps nature, and this is done in that which takes from the sun, that it may be more of the sun and glorified. In all defiled forms, so that a man follows the souls from himself, whatever is corrupted, the corruption is taken away. This happens because it takes from the sun and is glorified by natures to be repaired by virtues. Then from one turn let it ascend, even up to a thousand ways through the glass <note>original: "glam," likely "vitrum"</note> by ascent and descent, until such a supreme glorified clarity shall come that it is as incorruptible as the heavens. This is what it desires because it rules itself through God; they are one heaven where the whole world is made. Then the craftsman, through virtue, has the first [principle] and has this science to discern whether the Phison from which it came was subject to corruption, why it is clear, and that it will not be moist in itself like a tail, nor cold.

### Here begins the second book, called "On General Remedies"

<margin>First Remedy</margin>
Just as the first book, which concerned preservation, works with such power in the truth of the matter that through it a man can renew his life—and in this way it is meditated upon, for art indeed imitates nature. It will therefore be clear here that all things which seem to possess knowledge are made from the primary bodies correctly derived, speaking of the faculties of nature in which there is no doubt. For remedies of this kind are so much more powerful and wonderful than other things that through them, God will render all men <note>original: "dijs," likely a scribal error for "dis," meaning "to the gods" or simply "men" in this context of deification/restoration</note> capable, spirited, strong, and ready for all sufferings and labors.

<margin>Second Remedy for restoring the spirit to the lamb <note>likely a symbolic term for a state of innocence or vital purity</note></margin>
There is also "burning water" <note>aqua ardens; distilled alcohol</note>, which is a burning water <insert>Second Remedy</insert> in which the spirit of wine is reduced to the lamb. In the extraction of this, the spirit of wine takes on a flavor of its own; thus it takes hold freely in those sleeping, within whom it shall have cleansed the gold. Whether it pleases or not, everything can be done: let him drink it morning and evening as if in place of food. Then soon, within a few days, the spirit will come to such a state by itself that he will clearly feel himself returning to the strength and state from which he fell, and he will rejoice to have returned to his former health, or he shall remain unharmed in this state, provided it is used moderately and rarely. If it should happen that the spirit is moved only by being denied or cast down, he shall enjoy dominion over his own being in health. It is proven that he may worthily hold the state of his own good wine, as if it were diffused within, which now pleases and is said to be taken once freely.

<margin>Third Remedy: On the resurrection of the dead</margin>
In this second tractate, concerning the resurrection of the dead—that is, it is called the "Resurrection of the Dead"—you are always the thing. If you wish to help those for whom life in nature seems despaired of, as if they were beloved in the midst of death and destitute at the very point of life, standing dead in spirit though a slight pulse is still felt: then you may come to the aid of your "dead" so that they may quickly rise again, speak, see, and hear, if you wish, by the gift given by God. And especially, let the things of this resurrection be carried out boldly in such an event. Then, take it immediately and pour into the mouth that which shines with rays of valor; and then, even in desperate matters, it soon clearly strengthens and comforts. Even if he is failing, it will open the mouth instantly, and in the twinkling of an eye, so that he may see the illusions pass and be quickly converted. You must have the herb Celandine <note>Chelidonium majus</note>, whose flowers are all of a golden color; treat them through the clarity made manifest in the book, and with another fire, place any living flower in the fire. Immediately, in the instant in which he drinks, he shall rise up within himself and speak, and thereafter it comforts him with all supports, unless God wills that he finally die. And I tell you, this is only made manifest so that there be no suspicion in you; no other physician has reached this in practice, as is evident from the thing itself.

<margin>Fourth Remedy: On the cure of leprosy and other diseases</margin>
Since there are many kinds <insert>Fourth Remedy on the cure of leprosy and others</insert> of similar things, such as in other diseases, the plague of leprosy is detestable, a grave kind, abominable, difficult, and most to be dreaded. Anyone who dares to intervene knows that leprosy consists of those things which can hardly be cured unless the Divine Power speaks with us. If the plague of leprosy has issued from the corruption of nature, it is not for a lesser healer, but it is permitted—and I have said it is a wonderful thing to be in existence through one such as me. Then let the leprosy be worthily putrefied by this, and then the world within us, which has ceased to be from all being or has come to every kind of misery, shall be cleansed. And though it is now too difficult to cure from the spirit alone, if we intend to cure leprosy, then this thing is of value. If he is in such a state that he has become immovable, then read further in the books of the religious, where God left this to be cured for the salvation of those already mentioned, adding that gold—even if the place itself was too pressed—blows upon and comforts any leper for one hour, so that the place and all corruptions shall be renewed, and strength shall be born again. It comforts and balances everything in the mouth where the pulse is mentioned above, so that in every way in your dying soul, it says those things are prepared to serve God for you in this matter. This thing alone is what heals the aforementioned leprosy and returns one to God.

...it either totally extinguishes or dissipates [the illness] etc. I speak according to the great Arnaldus <note>Likely referring to Arnaldus de Villa Nova (c. 1240–1311), a famous physician and alchemist</note> regarding a great, useful, and manifest cure for leprosy; and certainly this water is like the flower and the best of all medicines for restoring [health] etc. That water, by celestial virtue, wonderfully cures leprosy and the itch <note>Latin: *scabies*, a term used for various skin diseases including mange or mites</note> in whatever way they exist. All swellings in this state are cured, and just as the water has much power for healing, it speaks of its virtue and acts, and one sends and applies it in whatever drink one desires most; and if one sends it in hot, then by the nature of this disease, the warm water by grace of medicine comforts and brings health and strengthens the nerves. Nothing like it can be found in the whole way, for this [disease] cannot linger because the water is a medicine and is adorned in itself. It is said here that God created it for the help of man, for this water, as it is said, strengthens and restores beyond all virtues in this world. And this water is made into the water which is called the "Water of Life" <term>aqua vitae: "Water of Life," usually referring to concentrated medicinal alcohol</term> and it is marked so that it enters the viscera as a medicine for infirmity. It will cure [the illness] of the elder tree and the garden, and then without doubt, if the disease is malignant, by sending it, it does not become impious but will heal. <margin>The best water</margin> This which has been said is wonderful; and if the "stropham" <note>Possibly a cramp or twisting of the bowels</note> grows warm, this water and the "palm" which is said to have power here, removes superfluity from the nerves and is called a medicine. And if there is malice gathered in them, then the best burning water is spoken of for them, because without doubt, once the burning water is removed in one month, the cure of the body follows unfailingly. It comes with much greater effect each time it is mixed, for it can be continued for two [doses] of the water, because it heals the disease of this world in a short time and is called a labor of cure. **The sixth remedy for skin eruptions.**

# On the Rectification of Medicine

The rectification <note>The process of refining or purifying a substance, often through distillation</note> is performed directly in this first stage. Because a single day is sufficient for human rectification through these means—as is said in the treatise *On the Trinity* etc.—or through another side. But these laxatives, once cleansed, purge all things toward themselves unless it is for teaching. And it is so that the cleansed things can be seen at the minimum, etc., when they have been in twelve laxations; and then the distillation is the result, and its liveliness is seen. And as they are then, they have within them sacred things and experience, as if it comes through itself by the **burning water**. 

Hence, he who wishes to cleanse things by loosening <note>laxando: refers to the chemical "opening" of a substance or a medicinal purging</note> does so not in many days, but in a few hours; for it must be done so that the spiritual part can prevail and flow. It could be, however, that the humors <note>The four bodily fluids (blood, phlegm, yellow bile, black bile) believed to control health</term> generated yesterday would be in a state of total evacuation; in such a case, the medicine is of the kind that must be sought through what is said concerning **burning water**. 

The wickedness of man does not permit him to reach this state in a few days. If you wish to know of this, it acts more in the "temple" <note>possibly referring to the head/senses or a specific vessel</note> when that medicine acts by itself. 

And I will give you an evident example: when there was an illness in the chest, and many humors in the body, and a blockage in the bowels, I used powerful vital **pills**. # Here begin certain extracts concerning the images of Ptolemy according to the twelve signs of the zodiac

The <term>Abrizabezken</term> <note>original: "Abrizabezken"; likely a corrupted Persian or Arabic title for a magical treatise</note> begins: namely, all the Easterners used to work with these images and did not care for others, but they observed that <term>Jupiter</term> <note>The planet associated with growth, kingship, and protection</note> should be in a masculine horoscope; and while they work in this way, the work shall be completed and shall reach their desired will once they are brought forth.

**To prevent a thief from entering a house:** Let a bronze image of a man be made whose rising face is <term>almazel</term> <note>original: "almazel"; likely a corruption of the Arabic "al-manzil" meaning a lunar mansion</note>, and then after this you shall say: "I bind every thief from this house through this image, because the spirit in it is the lord, and he shall not enter."

**To rule over fire so that it is not ignited:** Let an image of prey be made whose head is like the head of a sheep, specifically when <term>Mars</term> is in <term>Scorpio</term> under the degree of the horoscope of <term>Aries</term>; and with this prayer: "I bind the fire from this house lest fire be kindled in it, through this spirit of the image."

**So that a city may not be conquered:** Let an image be made of a man holding a sword in his hand, whose face is <term>almazel</term> while the horoscope is present, provided that <term>Jupiter</term> is over it; then [say]: "I bind this city so that the enemy may not storm it, nor a thief, under a certain part that is sent forth; certainly, in whichever of the enemies he is, he shall be [stopped]."

**To capture wild beasts:** An iron image of a man carrying a key in his hand, whose face is <term>Aries</term> while the horoscope is present, who shall be looking toward the face; let him first hold and touch the beast.

**Concerning a horse:** Let a lead image of a horse be made in the earth so that he [the thief or enemy] may not perceive it.

**To bind a sword:** Let a lead image of a girl be made in whose hand is a sword, in the earth, namely with <term>Libra</term> being in the horoscope which was looking toward the face; soon, when this is said, let the whole image be worked, and let not two [people] pass over it; the lead in which the image itself was buried should be placed underneath a small [spot].

### Observation through which knowledge and distinction are gained

Since Behethali says: When you wish to perform any work concerning images <note>term: "images" (imagines) - in this context, these are astrological talismans or amulets engraved with specific symbols at precise times</note>, know that the ancients produced for us in old books many images which work in the world, and in which there was skill, nobility, and experience regarding obstacles. ### Example regarding the destruction of regions
<margin>a</margin> There was a certain Jewish man <note>The text reflects common medieval tropes attributing powerful magic to Jewish practitioners</note> skilled in making an image for the purpose of destroying a certain region near the ends of the earth. Thus, that entire part of the region was being conquered by all its neighbors and was serving them, or rather they were ruling over the best of their kingdom. The land of his subjects was being laid waste by fires, robberies, and other invasions to such an extent that the king was unable to resist in any way, and thus he was often afflicted and suffered no small losses. Then the king, sending for the aforementioned Jew, had an image made. He took it and sprinkled it with blood and struck his own people, saying, "I myself shall destroy the sheep." Because he prepared it, he honored him and served him. Then, beyond measure, the Jew struck it until, by the movement, he brought forth the image so that it might bear [the curse]; and when he sprinkled it, that which was desired concerning the destruction of the kingdom came to pass, so that he brought his kingdom upon himself and afflicted it with many punishments. The king saw that he was in great misfortune, and sending for him, the Jew—by keeping that image—beheld the misfortune of the regions. And he spoke to them and spoke of the houses <note>Refers to astrological houses</note> he beheld, and he sent for him. Then the king was there and had placed him there; he said this, and the king replied: "I have seen how he beheld the fortunes in the regions, and still he beheld them." And he removed it; then he brought the fortunes, he looked and looked from the corners <note>The "angles" or pivotal points of an astrological chart</note> and wrote upon the image, not only of the region but of that man. And the king spoke, and he spoke to God, and he said: "There is no part of fortune that is not unfortunate." And also to many others, and he spoke of the kingdom in which one had seen and struck in one of the king's [places], and he had placed it within the image in such a way that it concerned the whole region, because he had gathered it from the four quarters—namely the East, West, South, and North—of that region. And he spoke to his people: "Henceforth, the image shall have destroyed the best of that king," and it was a great and wonderful thing.

**Centaury** <note>original: "Centaurea"</note>—this herb is said to have been discovered by the Centaur Chiron. When he had anointed himself with the blood of a vulture and afterwards washed himself in a jar of water, it stained <note>or "healed"</note> great wounds and abscesses <term>empyemata: internal collections of pus or abscesses</term>. It heals the colon and the feet; and if one wishes to play a trick with death, let this herb be placed in a fire, and it will seem as though the stars are running about everywhere. And if you apply it as a poultice to the nostrils while they are bleeding, the flow will be restrained immediately; and this is a proven experiment.

**Olcimia** herb—called *abanchis* by the Greeks and **Sage** <note>original: "Salvia"</note> by the Latins. When someone is asleep, if one prepares a clean glass vessel with water and "serpentine" <note>likely a reference to Dracunculus or a similar plant</note> and other things in the manner of a worm long before—just as someone loses blood from the chest in the blood of a vulture—if one speaks [the charm], it can happen that this herb appears horrific. And if a powder of it is placed on a stone and added [to a fire], it will seem that the whole house is full of serpents; these are the experiments.

**Ondonia** herb—called *alphoas* by the Chaldeans, *mithe* by the Greeks, and **Libera** by the Latins. This herb, as it is said, is gathered when the lambs are in the sign of Aries; it rejoices in its flock. One [dose] of the year cures all diseases. And if it is afterwards soaked in water for four weeks, whoever touches these worms will die immediately. And if some of the said herb is placed in dovecotes, all the doves will gather there. And if its powder is placed in a censer and used in place of incense and burned underground in a garden, herbs will immediately grow in it.

**Ovedonia** herb—called *agulonfoid* by the Chaldeans, *psyllis* by the Greeks, and by the Latins the **Rose** <note>original: "rosa"</note>. It is an herb with flowers like our wax. If it is taken with the powder of a weasel and this is blown toward someone, it will benefit them no further <note>possibly a reference to a binding spell or curse</note>. And if some of the said herb is placed in a net, fish will gather there. And if some of the said powder is placed in a lamp and lit, everyone will appear black. And if that powder is mixed for someone in oil, sulfur, and wine, and smeared on the mouth... the whole house will appear to be on fire.

**Vartadenia** herb—called *melle* by the Chaldeans, *vordisum* by the Greeks, and commonly **Inpylania** by the Latins. It has nothing of a sword <note>perhaps referring to the leaf shape</note>... and if it is bound between the teeth and placed in one's food, he will see and immediately know [secrets]. And if you place a mass of the purest silver near these things, and mix the aforesaid in the blood of a hare with the gall <note>correcting "melle" to "felle"</note> of a hare, all the hares will gather there where it has been placed.

**Omedonia** herb—called *de aguella* by the Chaldeans and **Broad-Dog** <note>original: "canis latus"</note> by the Greeks. They have praised this herb much more. If you obtain this herb in the sign of Leo, at which time secrets can be performed... if it is placed under dung for some time until a powder is made from it and placed in someone's milk at night, they will be able to sleep in the house until it is removed. And if you place it under dung with honey and four other red things, it will immediately draw [things] to itself. And if it is placed in a vessel containing cow's milk and placed in the skin of any cow, all the cows will follow.

**Edonia** herb—called *armilla* by the Chaldeans, *caapholi* by the Greeks, and **Serpentine** <note>original: "serpentina"</note> by the Latins. If this herb is mixed with the juice of basil, one will see red serpents. If a powder is made of these and placed on a stone, a wonderful multitude of serpents appears. And if this substance is placed under the head at night, one will not dream.

<column-break/>

The present book speaks of the virtues of certain animals, and first of certain stones which can be used in works <note>The "works" here refer to magical operations or alchemical experiments</note>. And first, it speaks of the **magnet**. The magnet is shining in color and is found in the Indian Sea and other parts of the East. Its attractive power is drawn from the force of the sea; if it is placed near its own kind, it embraces it. If it is cast into nitre <note>original: "nitro"; likely saltpeter or a similar mineral salt</note>, it moves directly toward it. Furthermore, if this stone is placed upon coals in the four corners of a house, and placed beneath those who are sleeping, they will all flee, and their goods can be stolen as one wishes.

If you wish to be **invisible**, take the stone which is called **ophthalmius** <note>original: "obtalmius"; likely the opal, which was historically believed to protect eyesight or grant invisibility</note> and wrap it in a laurel leaf. Then the color of that ophthalmius stone is not seen, for by its nature it is of many colors. And it is said that while all see it, those seeing the stone see it as if clouded; therefore it is called the "patron of thieves," for it seems to strike those watching with a "blind fist" <note>original: "pugno caeco"; a metaphor for a sudden loss of sight or confusion</note>.

If you wish to be free from all fear and terrible fantasies, take the **onyx** stone. It is black in color and is found in the Great Sea with respect to white veins; it comes from India into Arabia. If it is hung from the neck or worn on the finger, it shows that one is free from all fear, and especially from terrible fantasies and other things; this has been proven by modern men.

If you wish to **burn the hand** of someone without fire, or to make them flee, take the stone called **pithigen**. It is of a dark or scorched color, and if it is placed over the eye, it cures carbuncles <note>original: "antraxem"; an inflammatory skin lesion</note>. This stone constricts so strongly that it burns the hand, for it sounds like... <unclear>palyhu</unclear>.

If you wish to move the mind of a loved one toward joy and away from expense, take the stone called **sedatib**. It is born in the womb of beasts and appears to be of various colors, including white, purple, and green mixed together. It is found in the air and among various <unclear>amir</unclear>, and it is said to come from the physicians of dragons. If a second kind of sedatib is taken and placed under the tongue, it is said that all vain things are removed. If it is held in its proper hour and one thinks of a fair business matter while it is under the tongue, it is said that the matter will be accomplished.

<margin>Dyadochos <note>original: "Dyado"</note></margin>
If you wish for boiling water to cease immediately and not lose its heat, let the stone dry it out, or it leads to a parched throat. Then it is said, and if there should be one of its kind, it is because it is spoken of for the sake of others. And so it is said that the **Dyadochos** <note>A legendary stone said to resemble beryl; used in divination and summoning spirits.</note> is green, and according to our recipe, when it is cast into boiling water, it dries it up. It shall be done <insert>thus</insert> immediately: once the mass is cast in, it is drawn out. And let this be done by one of our seats through eating, and then they will pollute our [vessels] and the long duration of the suffering.

If you wish to provoke the hands of someone, take the stone which is called **Vegeum Medozis** <note>Likely a corruption of a stone name from Persian or Arabic lapidary traditions.</note>; one is black and the other is green. And if that stone which is black is placed in hot water and polished, and the water becomes more treacherous, they immediately perish. By moving it, one will come, and if he should be friendly, he will not lose what he wishes to see. If he has lost something and wishes to recover it, [let him use] the eyes and the stone, and it shall be as nothing.

If you wish that another should not feel pain nor any tortures, take the stone which is called **Memphites** <note>A stone described by Pliny the Elder, said to be found near Memphis in Egypt; used as a local anesthetic.</note>. This stone of ours is seen to come from the city of Memphis, and this stone is more sweet through all the sand. And <insert>it is through this</insert> that the stone is rubbed and mixed with water and given as a drink to one who must suffer some tortures. That drink induces such insensibility that he does not feel the blows nor the worthy tortures.

If you wish to create a fear of fire and for it to happen in all things, take the stone which is called **Celonites** <note>Also known as Chelonitis, the "turtle stone," believed to be found in the heads of tortoises.</note>. It is of a yellow color, and then it is said to bring on rains. If, however, that stone dries out more than the wood, it is seen as a moist, windy, fat wood, inescapable from itself; and thus the fat fire will be kindled.

If you wish to conquer all your enemies, take the stone which is called **Adamas** <note>Diamond or Magnetite/Loadstone.</note>. It is of a shining color and very hard, so much so that it cannot be broken except by [goat's] blood. It is born in Arabia or Cyprus <note>original: "dyo," likely a corruption of Cyprus or a similar locale</note>. And if it is bound to the left side, it rules over all enemies, wild beasts, untamed creatures, and men; and it dispels any quarrels, poisons, and all disturbances. Some have been able to climb with it.

If you wish to know many things to come and to have the wine of victory, take the stone which is called **Agates** <note>Agate.</note>. It is found in two [types] called white, and there is one better than it called Persian, which is similar to coral. It is born in the [islands?] and has great power. Our stone has long veins; let it be made a friend to the periwinkle <note>The plant *Vinca*, often associated with magic</note>, and it will live so that it is green, making a man pleasing and eloquent.

If you wish to obtain <term>merit</term> <note>original: "metusire," likely a corruption of "mereri" (to earn/deserve) or "mittere" (to send)</note> something from God, take the stone which is called **Allectoria** <note>Alectorius, the "cock-stone."</note>. It is a stone which, if inspected, is like water. It is drawn from the stomach of a cock that has been castrated for more than a year; some say after nine years. The best is that which is drawn from a weary cock. It is the size of a bean and can conquer even a King when held under the tongue; and he will desire that which is received with love.

If you wish to conquer before God, and the periwinkle conquers on earth and before God, then take the stone which is called **Amaraldus** <note>Emerald.</note>. It is the best for conquering all things, and it makes one conquer before God and gives the prophecy of interpretation.

If you wish to have good intellect and be unable to become drunk, then take the stone of **Amethyst** <note>original: "nethisto"</note>. It is purple and clear, and the best is found in India. It rules over all drunkenness and confers good sense and intellect in prophecy.

If you wish to overcome enemies and make lawsuits flee, take the stone which is called **Beryllus** <note>Beryl.</note>. It is of a pale color, clear, drawing toward clear water. It strengthens the body, overcomes all enemies, and puts lawsuits to flight. It is seen that it renders the one carrying it effective in all things.

<margin>Chalcedony</margin>

It is extracted fiercely from the head of a living dragon, and as they say, it drives away all poisons. If it is carried on the left arm, one conquers all of one's enemies.

If you wish to prove love between any two people, take the stone called **Aetites** <note>original: "aetites"; the "Eagle-stone"</note>. There are two kinds of colors, and it is called "Eagle" by some because the eagle collects these stones in its nest. It is found on the shores of the ocean. It is said to be found in the nest itself, and it is claimed that unless it is in the nest, there is hardly another stone that sounds within itself <note>Aetites were often hollow geodes with a smaller stone inside that rattled</note>. If it is bound by itself and suspended from the head on the left side, it brings about stoutness and affirms the matter. It overcomes wine and women, and it is said to increase love and grant victory to those fighting. It is bound to children who have been struck and brings them back. The Chaldeans say that if there is poison in the mouth, and it is placed in the mouth with a drink so that one can swallow the wine, the <unclear>pulsing</unclear> is said to stop immediately; and if water is given through it, it will heal.

If you wish to make a man safe, take the stone called **Jasper** <note>original: "iaspis"</note>. Because it is found in the sea, it is reddish and in every way green. It is carried by many according to where it is found. This jasper makes a man safe everywhere and restrains all pirate ships <term>dromones</term> <note>fast-sailing Byzantine warships</note>, storms, robbers, birds, clouds, and lightning from before his face. It is said that this is found from the first, and from whomsoever our things are. It is said to emit fiery rays like the sun; if it is placed in a double fever or in boiling water, it immediately takes away the heat and cools it in a short time.

If you wish for someone to be pleasing among his enemies, take the stone called **Hyacinth** <note>original: "iacinthus"; in antiquity, this often referred to blue sapphires or zircons</note>. There are two kinds of color: one has two natures and two red veins. It prefers to be set in silver. Some say there are two types: Hyacinth and Equatius. The Equatius Hyacinth is white like a sapphire with two flames; it is recognized by its red flames and by not having rain <note>possibly meaning it remains clear or dry</note>. It is said that if this is carried on the buttocks <note>original: "natibus"; a peculiar anatomical instruction common in folk magic</note>, then the bearer will be rendered pleasing and safe to the people in those parts, and he will perceive what is unique through himself; this brings wisdom.

If you wish to renew peace and concord, take the stone called **Sapphire** <note>original: "saphirus"</note>. Although it abounds in India, it is seen with flames in two ways. It creates peace and concord, and through it, it is said one prays to God. If it is offered in a house, it makes a man become lovable with love.

If you wish for a messenger to go and not have people know of it, take the stone called **Panis** <note>original: "panis"; literally "bread," but here a specific stone name</note>. It is known from the first desert island of Libya. Its ice <note>likely its crystalline structure</note> should be put into the earth in the nest where it is claimed to be. It is said that if anyone sees that stone, he is not seen, nor is he recognized by anyone in his actions, as the teachers say this consists of. But if it is offered in a house, it should be placed under such stones; it is said, however, to be carried around the neck.

# Here Begins Hermes

<margin>Gamba <note>Likely a reference to a specific authority or a shorthand for a constellation/sign, possibly "the Leg" or "the Shank."</note></margin> Hermes said that, after God, the Sun and the Moon are the life of all living things. For many whose birth <note>original: "nativitas"</note> was not chosen <note>i.e., not planned by elective astrology</note>, it is because the Sun and Moon are their ascendant; he looks toward them and delivers them from their divine life, lengthening it and strengthening all divine births by the benevolence of the Sun and the night through the Moon. ### Here begins the book on the behaviors and judgments of the planets, etc.

Now I shall begin the book on the behaviors and judgments of the planets. Know that a planet—whether retrograde, or weak, or weary, anxious, falling, and as if dead—is not in a single motion. One that is **Combust** <note>A planet "combust" is so close to the Sun that its power is said to be "burned up" or hidden.</note> is like a captive in a prison, in disgrace and without power in its state. One in **retrogradation** is like a healthy man from whom health recedes, but he remains fearful and <unclear>blind</unclear>. One standing **direct** <note>Moving forward normally.</note> is like a sick man recovering, who sees the approach of health. One that is **Depressed** <note>In its "fall," the opposite of exaltation.</note> is like fear between two enemies, <unclear>or</unclear> one who is between two misfortunes <note>The "malefic" planets, usually Mars and Saturn.</note>. One who is between two fortunes <note>The "benefic" planets, usually Jupiter and Venus.</note> is like a man eating sweets, returning from all evil and fear. One to whom misfortunes approach from the 10th house, or the fall itself, is like a man who already begins his own death, vengeance, and <unclear>enmity</unclear>. One whose planet is in the aspect of its enemy is like a man fearing his enemy. One who is with his enemy is like a man fighting with his enemy. One who is with a friendly planet is like a man who offers hospitality and is <unclear>full</unclear>. One who is in the house of his own power is like a man in his own power. A planet that is falling in the house of its exaltation is like a man absent from his own house and his own border. One who is in his own house or his house of exaltation while retrograde is like a sick man in his own house. One who is in his own house or house of exaltation [moving direct] is like a man in his own house whose directness and will are perfected, and he completes what he wishes to be done. One who is joined in his own house or house of exaltation is like a man who trades for his lord in his own house, or his king. One who has a ray <note>An aspect or beam of light from another planet.</note> is like a busy man in two [affairs]...

### Concerning the Change of the Air

Intending to focus specifically on the change of the air and wishing to know it better, I have investigated those things upon which it depends and through which the change of the air occurs. I have looked into those necessary matters which, by their own nature, are pleasing in themselves, and in their generations and applications <unclear>and</unclear> from which knowledge can be gathered. For one must know the signs which are in them, which the philosophers set down concerning the change of the air:

**Aries**, when it thunders and lightens, its first part causes rains and winds. The southern and fourth extreme parts generate and bring about mortality <note>likely referring to pestilence or "bad air" causing death</note> and they destroy; the southern parts generate and cool. **Taurus** holds a complex of both; where there is rain, it inclines toward heat. Its stars, especially those in the first part, are rainy and thus cause movement, winds, and clouds. In the middle, they cause humidity and cool; however, in the middle <unclear>elsewhere</unclear> they cause fires, lightnings, and thunders. **Gemini**, where they are temperate: in the first part they cause humidity and destroy; in the middle they are temperate; at the end they cause certain northern winds and thus movement; the southern parts ignite and generate. **Cancer** causes fourth-parts <note>possibly quarter-phases or specific intervals</note> that are feminine and hot, but in the beginning it makes the air hot and turbulent, and thus movement; those stars in its middle and at its extreme cause northern winds, and the southern parts generate. **Leo**, where it is hot and turbulent, makes the air and many rains and mortality; in its middle and extreme, they cause humidity and destroy; the northern stars are fiery and generate, the southern cause humidity. **Virgo**, where it is more humid and thunders, heats and destroys in its first part; in its middle and in **Gemini** and **Libra**, where it is thin, they foster rain; in its middle they foster the equinox and thunderous winds; the southern parts restore humidity and mortality. **Scorpio**, where it thunders and is fiery, causes excessive winds in the beginning; in its middle and at its end, the stars almost always cause movement. The Bow <note>The constellation Sagittarius</note> generates; the southern parts generate. **Sagittarius**, where it causes winds: the first part is humidity; in its middle and at its end it is fiery and the stars bring winds; the southern parts foster humidity and vary. **Capricorn**, where it is more humid: the first parts generate and destroy; in its middle and at its end it causes northern rains; the southern parts strongly generate humidity and summer heat. **Aquarius**, where it cools and is equinoctial in the beginning and bright in the middle; in the spaces at the end it is windy; the northern part generates, the southern causes excessive winds. **Pisces**, where it cools and causes winds: in its first part and middle they foster humidity, and the final stars generate; they cause northern winds.

### Here follows concerning conjunctions

<margin>If you wish to know about the conjunctions of the planets</margin>It should be noted that the conjunction of the planets is twofold, namely superior and inferior. The superior conjunction is of the three superior planets <note>Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars</note>. The inferior conjunction is of the four inferior planets <note>Sun, Venus, Mercury, and Moon</note>. It should be noted that the superior conjunction is fourfold: namely, the greatest, the major, the middle, and the minor. The **greatest conjunction** is when the three superior planets are joined, and this happens <unclear>rarely</unclear> <note>original: "anastaxila," possibly a corruption of a Greek term for a celestial revolution</note>; it causes the greatest and most admirable things because of the slowness of their motion, and through this conjunction it appears by itself—namely, that the conjunction itself destroys sects and laws and changes them; if it should act in such a likeness, it is the beginning of the destruction of certain lords. And if the conjunction of these three should be in the heads of their signs equally, then they shall be fortunate in their society. And if this conjunction was in a **fiery sign**, it signifies dryness; and if in a **watery sign**, it signifies the greatest rains; and if in an **airy sign**, it notes strength; and if in an **earthy sign**, cold is suspected. And if it was a conjunction of Saturn, being masculine, it signifies evil from the fear of men. 

The **major conjunction** is the conjunction of Saturn and Jupiter; this conjunction signifies new sects; if it began strong, it was a man, and he does not suffer what he has made, and it brings fear and tribulation. And their conjunction in a **fiery sign** signifies peace and society; but if in an **airy sign**, the greatest winds. In **watery signs**, however, there may be imminent rains and pestilence if it was hindered. 

The **minor conjunction** is the conjunction of Jupiter and Mars, and this signifies rain and clouds and ice, and also wars; and if the conjunction was then in the ascendant or in any angle, it shall act doubly, and all things [are affected] unless a fortune <note>A "fortune" refers to a benefic planet like Venus or Jupiter</note> has looked upon them. 

The **middle conjunction** is of Mars and Saturn, and this fights battle and wars and cruelties.

### Concerning Aries
This is a movable sign; when the Moon is in it, it is good to move from place to place and to do all things involving motion and to send a messenger, and he will return quickly. It is good to make a journey and to begin work, and all things that are done in fire are good to do and to procure. It is good to sail, to buy and sell fat things, to send a messenger, and to put on or be clothed in new garments. And if anyone begins an illness, he will be cured quickly. ### Concerning Taurus
Taurus is a fixed sign. When the Moon is in it, it is good to form a partnership, because it pertains to firmness and lasting a long time. It is good to build, to found, to buy vineyards, to plant trees, to sow, and to do all rustic works. It is good to hire male and female servants, to make a pact, to enter a house, and to lease a possession. It is good for a boy to take up a craft and letters <note>i.e., to begin his education</note>, and to enter a religious order. It is bad to begin a great journey by land or sea. It is bad to receive wounds, to perform bloodletting <note>original: "sanguine minue"</note>, or to send medicine to the hands. It is bad to speak with judges and princes; those who fall ill during this time will not escape it quickly.

### Concerning Gemini
Gemini is a <unclear>fce</unclear> sign; when the Moon is in it, it is good to treat friendships and to contract a marriage, if it is not for a firm pledge. It is good to take a physician, to go to fight, to set a boy to a craft, to sow, and to do all general things. Take on male and female servants, and do all things that ought to be completed quickly. It is bad to perform bloodletting from the arm, as Ptolemy testifies in the *Centiloquium*. Do not enter a house as a new possessor, but do put on new clothing. It is bad to sail by sea, nor should one do anything that ought to last a long time, or anything that is doubled in time.

### Concerning Cancer
Cancer is a movable sign. When the Moon is in it, it is good to perform bloodletting, to make or wash new clothes, and to take a fighter. It is good to make mills and water-works, to change one's reason and to move from place to place or change houses. It is good to put a ship in the water, to plow, to sow, to plant, to begin with a physician, and all things that ought not to last long. Whoever wishes to know the course of the planets should first know that the **Sun** completes its course every year, passing through all the signs by staying in each sign for 30 days. The signs are indeed 12, namely: **Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius, Pisces**. And on whatever day it is found after midday, the following day will be the second day, and it is called the "second first" day of the Moon.

Note this: that the Moon is always joined from that sign and from that degree in which it was during that hour in which it joined itself, and this happens in the day. If its conjunction is from one midday until the midday of another. And the Moon then moves from that sign and from all those signs afterward, just as the Moon is in a sign every day. The **fixed** signs, which are firm or stable, are four, namely **Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius**, because in these a thing lasts; thus it affects the body because the time in these is in its own [nature] and is not changed unless it be powerfully strong. Then there are four **common** signs <note>Also known as mutable signs</note>, namely **Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces**, in which the year is seen in Spring, Summer, Autumn, and Winter. It should be known that a person of this sort is both contemptible and grasping; because he wishes to take a portion from everyone, his greed <term>avaritia: the vice of greed or avarice</term> is directed toward the fire. Insofar as he is called "melancholic" <note>In medieval medicine, the melancholic temperament was associated with the element of earth and a cold, dry, and often bitter or greedy disposition</note>, he seems to be more than nothing in reality, and yet he carries within himself deceit and malice toward all his neighbors and friends. Even when he speaks with a man, he holds in his heart an evil will to harm and defraud him. Thus, he is seen to be the worst of men, sprinkled only with a superficial cleverness; when he speaks, it seems his words carry evils into the hearts of others. It is said that he is full of fraud and deceit, as has been proven by the experience of many.

For instance, if he has stinking breath <note>original: "anhelitum fetidum"</note>, it appears that the water within his inner parts is scarce, for just as water becomes corrupted where it is stagnant, so it shows in a bloated face and expression, perishing from the corruption of the interior. Thus, the truth is hidden from those who are among them, for the whole body stands and settles in this state, showing and guarding these things while leaving the damaged part in the water. It is said that the whole body must constantly be held by grace, lest those who fear little observe their own goods in him and thus cry out and speak; for speech is well known, and this is like water.

And yet, in his goodness, he is said to have a certain "simplicity" <note>here meaning a feigned innocence or plainness</note>; thus, if he is imbued with deceit and malice, it does not only appear in his face. This simplicity is noted in those who are accustomed to being perverse so that they may deceive others, acting as if they are good men even if they do not speak to men but see through them. Likewise, it should be known that he is full of ostentation, envy, and fraud, which is said to travel through a seven-fold path from which fraud does not exit. Envy is said to be a blood-red color, worldly and malicious. The envious and deceitful man shows himself otherwise through sidelong glances; he is greedy for those things which are directed toward his own end, and among those who cannot achieve this, he behaves as if he would snatch away whatever is most ready through that seven-fold path.

Furthermore, the fearful miser will never fill his heart with money; his heart is as large as a pot with a hole in it—whatever is poured into it, nothing remains there, but passes through and exits. So it is with the miser: in gathering riches and hoarding <term>thesaurisando: the act of storing up treasure</term>, he is never satisfied. He hoards and, as it seems, when he gathers out of envy, he desires even more to fill himself with money. Thus, he spares himself even more in food and drink, gathering gold, silver, and coins to fill his dwelling, which always seems empty to him. Then, though he fills his chests with money, he keeps himself in a state of poverty; he always thinks of money—how he can increase and aggregate it. He distributes nothing from it, but moves from evil toward others until he reaches hell, to be punished there and tortured with greater pains where they do not die. 

When such men serve the poor, they are afflicted and grieve; they do not truly share with them because they are unable to due to their greed. Their envy lasts until death in the works they see, and then, though they seem joyful of heart, there is nothing of rectitude or justice in them. Even if such a man gives his alms <term>elemosina: charitable gifts</term> with his whole mind, if it is done out of deceit and sickness—as is seen and heard—that alms-giving does not lead to salvation, but to the damnation of his soul. Let these things said concerning sinners suffice.

# 341. 471

To the praise and glory of the highest almighty God, by whose help the secrets of revelation are made clear for the enlightenment of those who lack the books published by the ancient philosophers. Alfonso, the most illustrious King of the Spaniards and of all <note>original: "hadasubie" - likely a corruption of Andalusia or related territories</note>, commanded this book to be translated with the greatest zeal and diligence from Arabic into Spanish. Then it was likewise interpreted <note>translated into Latin</note>; this work was completed in the year 1256 of Alexander <note>The Seleucid era</note>, in the year 1556 of Caesar at Rome <note>The Spanish Era, corresponding to 1256 AD</note>, and in the 6th month of the Arabs <note>Rebi I</note>. For the wise philosopher, noble and honored, Picatrix <note>The Latinized name for the author or the work itself, originally the Arabic Maslama al-Majriti</note>, compiled this book from 22 books and many other parts, and named it by his own name. In the name of the Lord, here begins the book which the most wise Picatrix composed in the magical arts from many books, as follows.

<margin>He is wise and powerful and to Him all things finally return</margin>
As the wise man says, the first thing we ought to do in all things of the world is to give thanks to God, for which reason it is said that He is to be praised. This is because He is the light revealing secrets, making known hidden things, and by His power He has made all invisible things to be known; in Him all things are open to everyone who calculates with judgment. I say, therefore, that the knowledge of His beginning is spoken of and desired; by His virtue and intellect all created things exist. By His power all things are created and renewed, and at the end they are governed by Him lest they perish. He is the one giving to things a power that remains unharmed forever within them, because He has no fixed place nor is He absent from them. For if He were not the "place" <note>a philosophical concept of God as the container of existence</note>, then in that time no natural things could operate, nor would their essences endure. Even though invisible things are infinite, His name is given there; may He be praised everywhere He is obeyed, as well as the prophets and saints who were enlightened by His beginning and showed the ways to men. By these ways, the gods <note>original: "dii" - likely referring to planetary spirits or celestial powers</note> are found by the wise, and then the spirits are said to be flourishing; may He receive us into His grace through merits and lead us to His eternal glory, Amen.

<margin>Picatrix</margin>
Since he wishes to focus on what the philosophers intended and to know the hidden secrets of magic, as is contained in the matters of magic which we have placed in these books, we are prepared to focus on why and how the invisible things of the magical art are known. One ought to know that they named this science <term>Wisdom</term> <note>original: "sapientia"</note> after all others, and indeed it is praised for its skill in hidden matters. Because they spoke of it and it reached us, we speak to the experts and to others through us; they did this for the sake of honesty and goodness, so that through this science men might be overcome by the habit of wisdom. Because of this, they spoke in it figuratively <note>using allegories or symbols</note> so that no one might be able to reach it unless they were enlightened by knowledge, just as God Himself leads the way in all desired things and provides the virtues by which one may reach that wisdom and fulfill <margin>intention</margin> one's desire in all things. Because I have finally compiled this book, and in this compilation I intend to explain the ways of this science and to provide a <gloss>commentary</gloss> on what the wise have spoken, I shall show that which they hid in other books where the words follow lightly. I, however, ask the highest Creator and Maker that this book does not reach the hands of the wicked, who are overcome by ignorance in the world, but let them keep it in mind. And since we shall work from it, we shall work for both good and for the best end of God. This book is divided into four books, and each of them is divided into its own parts. For in the first book, it speaks of the nature of the heavens and its effect through the <term>images</term> <note>astrological talismans</note> which are in it. In the second, it speaks of the figures of the heavens in general and the motion of the eighth sphere, and of the hours and their effects in this world. In the third, of the properties of the planets and signs, the art of figures and their forms in their colors, and how we speak to the spirits of the planets and signs through them, and many other magical things. In the fourth, of the properties of spirits and of those things which must be observed by virtue in this art, and how they are assisted in images, <term>suffumigations</term> <note>ritual incense offerings</note>, and other matters. According to the chapters of the first book: The first chapter is on the science of knowing at what level science and magic exist.

# The Twenty-Eight Mansions of the Moon

The work says more regarding this method, and it also describes the "where." It says you should do this in those specific days; it does not say by what virtue or in what degree, but it intends this for any station and for any of the works mentioned. Although it is necessary in the mansions themselves to perform the works of the mansion that one desires, it says in the first cause where you should take the degree in those acts which can be sent in those works. And for the present, it says the effect is intended from the works of the moon in those two mansions in which they are heartened <note>likely meaning "strengthened" or "aligned"</note>; wherefore it properly speaks of the 28 mansions of the moon and describes the properties of their mansions in order.

**The first mansion of the moon, which is called Alnath** <margin>Alnath</margin>
And it begins in the first minute of Aries and ends in the 12th degree and 51st minute; and the second time, according to them, the properties of the moon and the properties of the mansions are judged. Wherefore they followed the mediation of what the moon is said to do in this mansion: to make an image, one ought to provide in those images which he begins to make that he should first go into the essential things in that cause, and go into safety. He who must perform the work should provide for discord and enmity between a husband and wife, and between two friends so that they become enemies, and between two partners. Regarding the properties of this, place it so that the partners or whoever they may be shall flee from all humanity. And it shows you the way, saying in what foundation and in the observation of the two modes of help for the works; for it says that just as it can be for good and be safe and saved, so the works for the rejection of a party and conjunction in every evil work, so that the moon be in the rejection of the party, and for theft, or at least to snatch away the same.

**The second mansion of the moon, which is called Albotayn**
And it begins in Aries at the 12th degree and 51st minute, and it is said to go up to the 25th degree and 43rd minute in Aries. In this mansion, you may make an image for finding or for those who wish to dig wells and for finding hidden treasures; and it is permitted, it says, for the common good and for the destruction of houses and buildings before they are completed. And similarly, you may make in it an image to make everything valid for another, and it is so that it may be more strong and firm for all captives.

**The third mansion, which is called Azoraya**
And it begins in the aforementioned degree and ends in the eighth degree of Taurus, the 34th minute, though some say the 28th of Taurus. In this mansion, indeed, you may make images for saving those sailing by sea so that they may go in safety, and for the strengthening of all captives, and for completing the work of alchemy, and for all works which are of fire, and for hunting on land, and for placing affection between a man and a woman.

**The fourth mansion, which is called Albebaran** <margin>Albebaran</margin>
And it begins in Taurus in the aforementioned degree, namely the 8th degree and 34th minute, though some say the 12th; and its position is properly in the 21st degree of Aries and 24th minute, though some say the 25th. In this mansion, however, you may make an image for destroying a city, a town, or anything else you wish to destroy, so that it shall not be inhabited; or for destroying a toll-gate, and for hiding a theft, and for placing discord between a husband and wife, and for corrupting fountains and wells and those which once held treasures, and for killing <note>original: "m'ificand'", likely *mortificandum*</note> and for binding all reptiles and individual poisonous animals.

**The fifth mansion of the moon, which is called Almicam** <margin>Almicam</margin>
And it begins from the 21st degree and 25th minute (or 24th) of Aries and Taurus, and ends in the 4th degree and 17th minute (or 10th), though some say of Gemini. In this mansion, however, you may make images—provide for the young—for learning arts and crafts, and so that those going out may go as they wish, and so that those sailing may go safely, and for killing <note>mortifying</note> from the earth, and for destroying the concord of a wife, and for placing benevolence toward the wicked and a wife; and this according to what was in the first mansion of the variants. And here it was for the scales <note>Libra</note> and Aquarius.

**The sixth mansion, which is called Alchaya**
And it begins from the 4th degree and 17th minute (or 10th), though some say of Gemini, up to the 17th degree of Aries and 8th minute (or 36th). In this mansion, however, make images for destroying cities and towns, and for the young regarding arts, so to weight them that the enemies of Kings are strengthened in their works of vengeance, and for crafts, and for destroying trees, and for diminishing friendship between two persons, and for killing <note>mortifying</note> hunters on the way, and for dispensing medicine so that those taking them shall not work freely.

**The seventh mansion, which is called Aldirah**
And it begins from the 17th degree and 8th minute (or 36th), though some say of Gemini, and it ends in the end of Cancer. In this mansion, you may make images for increasing merchandise, and before the moon so that it may go toward the good. And for increasing wages, and so that those sailing in water may go healthily, and for placing friendships between friends and partners, and for driving away flies so they do not feed whenever you wish, and for crafts and for gifts for all those going before kings and others, for any work, and for making medicine for favor...

And observe their moderation and their harm, such as from the aspect of the fortunes: for if the ascendant is in the diurnal signs and a fortune is in its twelfth [house], the work is destroyed, as is the month. ->To create love<-

When someone desires to place love between two people so that their love may be lasting, let images of both be made in their likenesses. Let this be done in the hour of Jupiter or Venus, and let the Head of the Dragon <note>The North Node of the Moon, considered highly auspicious</note> be in the ascendant. Let the Moon be with Venus and behold her with a good aspect, and let the lord of the house of the ascendant behold the lord of the first house with a trine or sextile aspect <note>Harmonious astrological angles of 120 or 60 degrees</note>. Afterward, join them together in an embrace and bury them in the place of one of them; they will love each other and have lasting love in their hearts. This is called the "Figure of the Most High" of which Ptolemy speaks in the book *Centiloquium*, aphorism 33 <note>original: "verbo 33°"</note>, and we have spoken of this in the fourth book of this work, in the volume where we shall explain it as you desire.

### Image for generating love between two people
You shall make two images in the ascendant and the first face of Cancer, with Venus in it and the Moon in the first face of Taurus and in the eleventh house. When you have made the images thus, you shall give them embraced and bury them in the place of one of them; they will love each other and have lasting love in their hearts. This is called the "Figure of the Most High" of which Ptolemy speaks in the book *Centiloquium*, aphorism 33, and we have spoken of this in the fourth book of this work, in the volume where we shall explain it as you desire.

### Image for lasting love
Make two images and place Fortune <note>The Part of Fortune</note> in the ascendant and the Moon in Cancer near Venus. Write on one image this name *Alghossim* and for 220 ways <note>Likely a numerical or kabbalistic reference</note> those same figures on the other image, and 8 and ways, and join both as if embraced; then a lasting love is completed between them.

### Image so that nobles, kings, or whomever you wish may love you
You shall make images in the hour of Jupiter and in his name. In it, place Fortune in the ascendant, and let Fortune be strong, not falling, retrograde, or combust <note>Terms for a planet being weakened by its position or proximity to the Sun</note>. Let the lord of the ascendant be strong, in a good state, and in the power of its exaltation. Let the 10th house behold the lord of the ascendant with a trine or sextile aspect with strong reception. Let the lord of the ascendant be in a commanding sign and the 10th house be in an obedient sign. Whoever has this image with them—the one who carries it—will be loved and honored, and whatever he seeks from his lord and in time, he shall have it, or from those to whom he is committed.

### Image so that a lord may be loved by his men and they obey him always
You shall make two images when one part is in the hour of Jupiter and the Moon is beholding the Sun with a good aspect and separated from the misfortunes <note>The "malefic" planets, Saturn and Mars</note> in the ascendant. Place the Head of the Dragon in the ascendant. Then make another image where the ascendant is the fifth house from the [first] ascendant, and this in the hour of Venus. Let the Head of the Dragon be in the ascendant and let it behold the ascendant itself with a good aspect, and this in the hour of the Moon, and let the Moon be free from misfortunes. Bury the image of the ascendant of some of the servants in the house of the lord, and with this, they shall become lovable to their sudden friends.

### Image so that a servant may love his lord
Let two images be made, one of which is made in the hour of some planet [pleasing to the lord], and let the ascendant be in the houses of one of the planets pleasing to someone. Let the Moon behold the Moon, and the Head of the Dragon be in the ascendant and in the 10th house. Make the second image in the hour of the inferior lord, whose ascendant is the house of the aspect of the other where he now dwells. Let the Tail of the Dragon <note>The South Node, usually considered unlucky but used here for binding</note> be in the ascendant and in the 10th house. When you have made these two images thus, join them to embrace each other and bury them in the place of the one who seeks the love of the other.

### Image for obtaining dignity from a lord
You shall make two images with a fortunate ascendant and its lord. [Keep] the unclean ascendant and the unclean [parts] further removed in fortune from the ascendant and its lord. Place a misfortune in the eleventh house beholding the ascendant and its lord; let them behold the lord of the ascendant in turn with a good aspect with reception. Then let him who perseveres thus keep it with him, carrying it so that it is seen by no one; then in the presence of the lord, whatever dignity or office he seeks from him, he shall have.

### Image for increasing riches and merchandise
You shall make images with a fortunate ascendant and the lord of the house, and [place] them in the manner of the lord and the lord of the house of the ascendant, and the lord of the house in the 10th, and the lord of the second house, and the lord in the 2nd house. Let the lord of the Part of Fortune be in such a house, and place the Part of Fortune in the ascendant or in the Moon. Let the lord of the Part of Fortune behold them with a good aspect, being fortunate. Let him keep the thing to be done within himself from one part of its lord; let him guard them as he intends them to be made so that they are seen by no one, and he shall profit in every deed and shall have gain from others at all times.
