# An Image to Increase Love or Sorrow
To make images fortunate, you must establish the 2nd house and its lord, and ensure a fortunate planet <note>original: "fortuna"</note> beholds it. This should pertain to the lord of the 10th house and the lord of the Ascendant. Let the lord of the Ascendant be fortunate and let a fortunate planet behold him; likewise, let the lord of the 10th house, the Moon, and the lord of the Moon's house be fortunate. Complete this image so that the lord who makes it is in the middle of it. Place it, and it shall be done.

### <insert>An Image for Destroying Cities</insert>
If joined under the hour of Saturn, because he is an ill-fortune <note>original: "infortuna"</note>, with the Moon waning, or if the ill-fortunes are in the Ascendant and at the lord of the Ascendant and the lord of the house of the Ascendant. You should remove the fortunate planets from the Ascendant in its house and from the lord of the Ascendant. By this arrangement, through the public state of the place I speak of, you will see wonders.

### <insert>An Image to Flee from a Place Greatly</insert>
Make an image in the form of that market or place which is desired, in the hour of the Moon, with the Moon increasing and in a swift course, separated from the ill-fortunes. Place the lord of that place in the Ascendant, or make the image of the lord of the Ascendant and its lord.

### <insert>An Image for Catching Many Fish</insert>
Albanum says in a certain book of this art, which he himself proved, that it was captured in time. You should make an image in the figure of a fish and cast it. Make the fish when the Ascendant and the Moon are in aspect to one another. Do this in the hour of the Moon. When the image has been so fashioned, cast it into the river where you wish to fish, and you will see wonders, for a multitude of fish will gather in that place.

### <insert>An Image so that a Fisherman May Profit</insert>
Make an image on a tin plate of a man sitting in a chair having the work of a fish. Make another image of a man standing, pushing into it, having a net with many fish in his hands, and let these images pertain to one another. Make both images under the Ascendant of Taurus or Libra, with Mars in the Ascendant. When this is done, place these images in the place where you wish the man to come, and you will see wonders: people coming to that place.

# An Image for Healing <insert>Pain</insert>
Make an image of a lion on a plate of purest gold, holding a stone in its paws as if it were crushing it. Let it be made in the hour of the Sun, with the lord of the face of the Lion ascending. Whoever beholds this tablet, it will immediately free them from pain. This has been most wisely proven. Hermes <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary founder of alchemy and astrology.</note> adds to this construction of the lion image that the Moon should not be beholding the lord, nor should it be beholding Saturn or a ray from him.

# An Image to Place Love Between Two
Make two images when the fortunes are increasing. You shall make the Ascendant and the 10th house fortunate, and remove the ill-fortunes from the Ascendant. Place the lord of the house as a fortune, beholding the lord of the Ascendant. Understand this perfectly: a trine aspect <note>original: "aspectu sub 3o" - an astrological angle of 120 degrees, considered very harmonious.</note> completes the union. A sign of Fire does not behold another except by the same aspect, and a sign of Earth likewise. The same is to be understood of the signs of Air and Water. By a trine aspect, perfect friendship is completed; a sextile aspect <note>60 degrees</note> is for middling friendship, because the signs agree in the nature of Air. A quartile aspect <note>90 degrees, often considered tense</note> is also for middling friendship. Now let us return to the proposed work: I say, make the image if it be for two friends, or let it be for the lord of the 11th house <note>The house of friends and hopes.</note>. If it be a man and wife between whom friendship is desired, let it be the lord of the 11th house. Make the lord of the Ascendant have a good aspect and receive a good reception from the other. Place the images in the place where friendship is sought, and there will be friendship.

# An Image to Increase Favor with a King or Another
Make two images, one of which you make in the hour of Jupiter with a favorable Ascendant and the Moon beholding them. Place them in the Ascendant or the 10th house. Make the images so that they behold each other or the Moon, and let the fortunes be ascending. Let the lord of the Ascendant behold the lord of the other by a good trine or sextile aspect. Fashion them as if embracing each other, and let it be proven in the place of the person who wishes for the king's favor.

### Image for destroying a city
Fashion an image <note>Latin: *ymago*; in this context, a talismanic figure made of metal, wax, or clay</note> in the form and likeness of that which you desire [to destroy]. Do this in the hour of Mars while the Moon is in Scorpio. ### Image to hinder buildings
Fashion two images, one of which should be made in the hour of the Sun with Leo in the Ascendant (its exaltation), and the other in the hour of the Moon with Taurus in the Ascendant. Let the Moon be in the Ascendant with light and safe from misfortunes. Until you take them away—and when you show these beneath the earth—at that very hour they shall remain, and the buildings shall be hindered.

### Image for following a ship
Fashion the image you desire in the hour of the Sun with Leo in the Ascendant, the Moon falling away from the Ascendant, and removed from Mars falling from the Moon. ### Image to put bees to flight from any place

# On the Moon and the Animation of Images

When the work is begun in the **Moon**, when it is favorable for the task, do not let it be done without **Diamond** <note>original: *adamante*</note> and **Adamas** <note>likely a repetition or distinction between the gem and the magnetic loadstone</note> by the rays of the hours and the higher powers. ### The Philosophy of Talismans
These works were especially the **saying of Aristotle** <insert>saying of Aristotle</insert>. And he says that images which do not have a spirit are external and unsuitable, for they were not fit to receive the aforementioned spirit. **Azeles** <insert>Azeles</insert> <note>likely a reference to a specific Arabic or Hermetic authority, possibly Al-Kindi or a similar sage</note> says in his books that this comes to us better and more highly than what they have, and it comes from the full [heavens] as an invaluable thing; for when a fortune appears, he wishes the returning spirit to be perceived by the soul. In trees and composite bodies, there is a greater power and lordship because of the stars and the soul <note>The "soul" here likely refers to the *anima mundi* or the vital spirit believed to inhabit all physical things</note> which they receive. Concerning your true intent and the matter for which you come, let it be done with caution. When the ascension is direct and the <unclear>aspect</unclear> <note>The geometric relationship between planets</note> is in harmful works, you should place the sign of the lord of the petition and the reception directly in the aspect. ### The introductory rules of the art follow as below

In all works that you wish to perform for love and goodwill toward a man or woman, see that the Moon is received by Venus, Jupiter, or the Sun. Let its end be in its own house or in its exaltation. And note for the trine aspect <note>original: "trigono aspectu"</note> which touches the sides equally so that any side has one hundred and twenty parts <note>120 degrees</note> through which you perceive the heavens. And know that what joins in a square figure <note>original: "figura quadragona"</note> through equal sides has 90 parts in any part of itself by the circumference of the heaven. And know that the aspect of the quadrangle is constituted of four equal sides and in the concavity 90 parts of the circle of the heaven. Opposition, however, is as it was in the pairings of the diameter of the heaven. 

When you wish for a matter in which I was lingering to be long-lasting, so that something you work on cannot be retracted, wait until the Moon has been received by Venus in its first aspect, and received by Jupiter or by its two lords, Jupiter or July <note>likely a scribal error for "Solis," the Sun</note> by aspect. And thus finally he does this better through the heavens, Jupiter, Venus, and Fortune, away from Jupiter and from worldly misfortunes. 

And if your work is for love and goodwill, place the lord of the ascendant, Jupiter, and the lord of Venus. If your work is to acquire hereditary things, place the third lord, Venus, in the first part of the house. And if your work is to look toward a person of the laws, let it be in the ninth house. And if your work is of trust, so that it may be through thoughts and labors, let this be in the second house and in a strong place for the fortunate ones; the messenger of that fortune is the god, the proper lord received by the fortunes. 

And if your work is of petition, disputes, and many things, he makes the aspect with Mars received by the Moon with a consenting aspect. And if your work is for arranging debts, make the receiver of Saturn in the place of Mars. # On the Nature of Divination and the Prophetic Soul

Through those things which he himself perceives by augury <note>original: *augurio*; here referring to the interpretation of signs or omens</note> through sight and hearing, and by reflecting upon those matters proper to augury and through their power—in which they are also formed—he was strong and pure in shaping within himself those things which are the very operation of the world above in the spaces from which all things proceed through causes. He both hears and sees much, and this he attains—or wishes to be attained—through himself; and the pure, true things which belong to the essence of the whole world, from its own strength. Through this, he knows and sees without the [ordinary] power in which all things are formed. He sets aside harmful things and leaves behind all outward worldly matters, from which only that which is currently visible is drawn away; and in turn, it is seen through himself, as if through dreams of augury. 

That is to say, if there are dreams from evil spirits, they are purged, and he does not apply them to himself. Then, whoever sees is seen, and it is said that if they are celestial dreams, then it is both well and pure, and achieved through divining. And so it is said against those [evil] things, and those things which they perceive are applied. From the purity of the soul comes the skill <note>original: *peritudo*</note> in which the things he desires are formed, and the things received are unlocked, and he understands them well. I mean this as if while waking; and through that which is so described, in which they are formed, and this is from a soul polished and clean from superfluous vices and impurities. From this, things follow just as if they are beings appearing through the intellect, and they reveal their causes in the intellect, which is the receiver and the applicant. Through this, he is a diviner, perceiving through himself things abstracted from the event; whereby he reaches the things he perceives through himself, which in nature are pure through themselves. It is not then [merely natural], but rather he perceives and sufficiently makes other things seen. 

And if [he reaches] the higher realm alone, and if God himself held more perfect things with the prophet—and this cannot happen except in a man individually, in whom the prophet is first seen to be fulfilled by the One who is separate—it is He who first sends forth the prophets and infused his own mind into him. God himself wills it in him; it is revealed and certain through whom it happens thus. And through this, one knows well the intention of man; and God himself, it is said, is seen. Because they know all things, but then through the "bond of the world" <note>original: *ligamentum ipsius mundi*; a Neoplatonic concept referring to the connection between the spiritual and material realms</note>—that is, above the second [level]—and through this he reaches all the celestial powers forming things. He is called a prophet because, through himself and for another, he is more fulfilled and more fortunate in certain things. 

And this is also for seeking, so that he may arrive at things—may he arrive, he does arrive, he reaches them effectively. For we do not only wait for things as a man [waits for] the form of the world; and anything teaches us to have good morals and to desire the good, lest a man be carried away by the manner of evil men. Therefore, man is taught in the laws and the eloquence of the saints, so that through the tradition of the good, they may find themselves among the good. And this is the way and the method of reaching, through a fortune greater than nature <note>original: *fortunam maiorem natura*; referring to a supernatural or divinely granted success</note>, and of knowing the things of the world. And they are so called because, through themselves in the equality of nature, and then through themselves by these things, it is seen through what is then called [prophecy]. Just as it is said of others: through ourselves we learn, and even more, we come to mathematics through ourselves, in which the whole of man is fulfilled through speculation. 

And through these things there is also the good that every man born into the world has, with a part for discovering, who is then called "fortunate" better than [the ordinary]. He says this in the book *On the Mansions of the World* <note>likely a reference to a specific astrological or cosmological treatise</note>: what is said from above is seen to be the way and the path, not otherwise. And through this way of perceiving and reaching those things through a greater fortune—such as are morals and virtues—which [guide] men. And because through these things one can reach [the goal] here in these two, before all else, they fall into essence: one level of reading and a durable property, though in perpetuity and without end. And so God assigns the grades of the law, which we see from life—a life worthy of being remembered—unless it be another life from whence it had been, either life through itself or through the intellect. 

But let us now return to the proposal: as we said, through the power of a better soul, it is seen through itself so that they may be corrected and hear us, and become such that he loves those he willed and hates those he willed through himself. And through this, [he acts] rightly from the effects he willed; and this is the operation of the soul through itself, through the spirit, which it performs in images. It is spoken of through "figures of rectitude" in which man is seen, and all things, and those things which he seeks are to him as if they are right through the images themselves. And through this, the operation was partly as if pure, and fully pure, and clean.

They work because they return to that same part as material and a disposition for receiving another form. And this happens because some matter having a form and figure cannot receive another form unless that which was previously disposed to receive a form is first given up and lost; and thus it receives it. ### Chapter Seven: On the method of making images, finishing them, and how many parts must be made within them:

From what we have said so far, it appears clearly enough how the form is received and how its matter is provided through its discovery. For the image and the reception seem to be made of one and the same nature of similarity and diversity, flowing from the material of invention and out into the object. For this work, the image requires a similarity to the effects of the stars and the appearance of the metal from which it is composed, as well as the place and time where such an image is finished. It is clear by what causes the invention occurs; if a multitude appears around it in a single effect, and if it is diversified over a long time, it will fail by itself. From this, it appears that the cooperation <note>Latin: *coadiuuatio*; referring to the alignment of natural and celestial forces</note> is like a wave moving toward the acquisition of the effect of the magical art.

I say, therefore, that if similarity is the cause of its creation—because it works a division within itself according to its primary division—it is divided into two parts. Just as there are parts regarding the genera and differences of beings in which they are generated, it is also divided into parts that are within the surface of its body. The "place" is the quantity of carrying toward two parts, namely into one and one, from which those quantities seem to be parts in one according to "more or less" in the best way. Just as a line is the matter in one, from which the aspect is seen, they are symbolized in another where it is not looked at outside of that which receives the effect into a unity of similarity or dissimilarity. 

A line is also spoken of through "water" <note>Likely a metaphor for the fluid transmission of influence</note> in this place of division; the line brings one thing. And just as we divide the division according to the end, we speak of the "plane" regarding a straight line. This is said because although it has two points placed within it, one toward the other, this is said to be more "leveled" <note>Latin: *aplanari*; to make smooth or flat, a technical term for preparing the talisman's surface</note> than all others. It is called "one" because any straight line upon which a thing moves is arranged in one limit and in one primary aspect; the first point of the line, through another most unknown division, reaches to the other point directly opposite it. The cause of division in such things is to induce the whole. 

And this is because for this other elementary thing, its end ceases in a straight line and holds the power of the points because of the rays of the planets. These rays lead to infinity through a single point on the surface of the body arranged to receive the points of such rays. The cause of its end is in a single time, namely the stellar configuration that is sought for the effect. 

From this, another thing must be known: how many times the metal must enter into the object or the composite thing to capture the effect through the order of effects. Each thing, by its similarity, appears to be divided. Since the line of aspect is spoken of as one of the forms, it must be a single whole for the universe, so that it may be "complete and leveled." For if the said line were crooked, it would certainly be weak and diminished. The surface is one in the figure of the given object. This is because the surface is the extension of the effect in a single line in its place. 

Then, since no one can be extended simply, I say that what is extended in matter is the surface. Because it is fitting that "water" <note>The receptive medium</note> receives many things in itself—heat, cold, moisture, scent, colors, and other such things—and without the influx of the line, it is no longer joined. Even if it comes from a single soul-image, the surface acts toward this. I say, therefore, that you should understand the secrets and the distance; the cause of the "what kind" and "how much" of those acting in such a way, since the image must be made in a short span of time. 

It is also necessary to know that one of all works follows the motion of the [celestial] body, just as leveling divides the effect in one. According to this, the division of the thing by parts in the effects in one matter is divided by the time of the aspect, according to the place in which it is to be given and influenced. If the end is not reached so that the work is completed, it is because of the many declining planets. 

And this is to look at the time in the due and competent hour, and to know the conjunctions it has with any of the planets, whose aspect might be in one degree or in some other opportune aspect—such as a trine <note>An astrological aspect of 120 degrees, usually considered very favorable</note> or others—to be leveled for those things necessary for this work. By considering the efficacy of their complete and incomplete effects from the locations of the planets, according to the mode and form of working, one must discern whether they are full of rays, or descending, or in their exaltation <note>The position in the zodiac where a planet's influence is most powerful</note>, or in what place the influence is to be given. For they are increased in their forms so that they may inform [the matter]. 

Since there are many points of light and darkness in the spheres, as is said in astronomy, this is a most useful secret in magical doctrine. According to the usage and mode of those dividing, as it is said, in similarity and property: this is the time for looking at what kind of effect is given. Time and place are the final things in this end.

Man is of the world and a matter of a better manner because they are tempered by God, not from a subtle sum of other matter. And therefore these things follow by a skillful mastery, and they are compared to a divine essence; and they are finally composed. These are like a medium, and others are apparent, yet they are not simple but consist of a composite. As it is said in the seventh part, it proceeds from the beginning up to the 28th part. 

I wish here to give an example, not to make it plain of itself but through a divided and first explanation with a better example: while not simple, they are heat, cold, moisture, dryness; and the first are not composed, but are hot, moist, dry; and the second are hot and dry, hot and moist, cold and dry, cold and moist. And then they are not of themselves the things found: fire, earth, air, water. And others are composed, namely the seasons: Spring, Summer, and Autumn; and four are composed, namely the four humors: blood, choler, phlegm, and melancholy. And the sixth are apparent, being tempered in life and old age and the "forest" <note>prime matter</note> mentioned before. For heat, cold, moisture, and dryness are similar to the time, the air, the water, and the earth in their mixed parts, summarized and subtly divided. For he is called "hot" because he is hot and dry; he is called "hot" then because he is one, not because he is composed of fire in some way. And every composite is such as it is from the things preceding it and named, from which they are composed: as heat proceeds from moisture and coldness from water and dryness from earth. But man is called the first and principal sum. And man is not [defined] only in the four lungs, gall, heart, head, or in the hands and all other members, but heat predominates from the motion of the heavens, and coldness from its opposite. The four things found—earth, which moves against the first motion—from which all generations in all matters must derive, from the seeds of the earth. Heat is in all things with the four seasons, the composition of matter, and motion, since heat is the effect of the sum of the thing of which we speak. In this way, these seeds of matter are from the same sum, and thus they are seen to be in man and in all things in those apparent subtleties. If you wish to work in these other and nobler things from which [knowledge] is commanded, you will find no case more pure; they are in the subtlety of matter and the highest of the superior, because you wish to reach the ultimate unity. And because they have been placed until now in the ultimate mixture and joined to such a superior God, I cannot simply explain and arrange them further, but I will make you benevolent and attentive in the aforesaid second part.

Engrave these figures upon a stone above. **An image for keeping away owls** <note>original: "bubones" - can also refer to swellings or buboes, but in this context of pests, "owls" or "horned owls" is the traditional translation.</note>
But with the face of Jupiter ascending, then place the stone in the location
where you wish, and neither owls nor horned owls will be able to come
to that place any longer as long as the stone remains there. **To put flies to flight**
Engrave these figures on a plate of iron with the Earth ascending in the face of Scorpio; this plate
you shall place in whatever location you wish and the flies
will recede from that same place, and they are these: <image-desc>Three red sigils: a crescent-like shape, a vertical line with a loop, and a 3x3 grid with circles at the nodes.</image-desc>

Engrave these figures so that a friendly man may come to you:
first the lines which you see, and in the hour of Venus with the second face of Jupiter
ascending, he shall come there with the Moon waxing; in that hour write the name of the man you
wish to come to you, then take the head of a hoopoe <note>A bird frequently used in medieval magic for its supposed occult properties.</note>
[wrapped] in a linen cloth [and put it in] the fire, and immediately he shall come to you. <image-desc>A series of red sigils resembling the letters W, H, X, and M with small circles at the terminals.</image-desc>

**To place envy between certain people as you wish**
When you wish to distract two men so that, as I say, they [cease to] love one another, make the
figures written below on the tooth of a black dog in the day and hour of Saturn, with the Earth in the face of Capricorn
ascending, with Saturn there waxing; place that
lamina <note>A thin metal plate or inscribed object.</note> in the place of one of them or in the place where
they are accustomed to gather together, and it will dissolve their friendship.
A leaden plate for it. **To bring misfortune to any place you wish**
Engrave these figures on a leaden plate with the brain of a hoopoe in the day and hour of Saturn,
the second face of Capricorn ascending with Saturn present in it;
and place the plate in the location you wish to destroy and perish so that
the [influence] of Saturn pours into it, and [leave it] there as long as the plate remains. <image-desc>Red sigils including a crescent, an X, and a Greek sigma-like character.</image-desc>

Know however that this work ought to be done when the tooth is full <note>Likely referring to the moon's phase or the "fullness" of the astrological timing.</note> when it sits better, then it
was quiet; and make these figures which are for a friend, namely to act as if you did not know this;
then some wise man was in many places, since in this book on this page, look:
place [them] with discretion. **Chapter Two: Concerning stones, apply them as to the eyes and
concerning the formation of figures.**

These things indeed we intend to make clear: namely, which planets are in which metals and
stones, and also the figures of the planets and their many works to be joined; and first:
<margin>**Concerning Saturn**</margin>
Saturn has from the metals iron, and the "hand stone" <note>original: "petram manum"</note> from the stones, also diamond and others
[such as] *tamasse* and *nechechate* <note>Transliterated Arabic or technical terms for specific minerals.</note> and *elaur* and *senet* and *almagmac*, and as he has in
red stones and in golden marcasite in the second [face]. <image-desc>Red sigil resembling a stylized H.</image-desc>
<margin>**Concerning Jupiter**</margin>
Jupiter from the metals has lead <note>Note: Usually Saturn is lead and Jupiter is tin; the scribe may have swapped these or followed a variant tradition.</note> and from the precious stones white and golden ones, and the stone
unto this in emerald and in coral and in crystal and in all white stones and
clear and shining ones in one, and in gold. <image-desc>Red sigil resembling a stylized F.</image-desc>
<margin>**Concerning Mars**</margin>
Mars from the metals has [copper], from the red and all kinds of sulfur, and he has as if from glass and

The Sun from the metals has inscribed glass and the magnet, and has from the stones asbestos and
diamond and red horn and all stones shining and clear, and as he has in *sedina* and
*azumbedich* and *colri* and balas ruby and Syrian pearls and gold. **Concerning Venus**
Venus from the metals has red copper and as in silver and glass, and from the stones lapis lazuli and
coral and from *lyenoch* and as in *alanche* and in *almagmac*. <image-desc>Red sigil resembling a stylized X.</image-desc>
<margin>**Concerning Mercury**</margin>
Mercury has from the metals quicksilver and as in iron and glass, and from the stones he has emeralds
in precious circles, and has as in *arumbedich*. **Concerning the Moon**
The Moon from the metals has silver and from the stones silver marcasite and others in turn,
and as she has in crystal and in azure and in *alassa* and in *almeche*; these were below, namely for the planets,
and especially from Saturn; here he was strongly inspired, he found [how] to join the stones, both in the book
of herbs and in the books of spirits and the hours for the image which are in the wise science, and so it is.

# The Forms of the Sun and Venus

The form of the Sun, according to the opinion of <unclear>Eretenis</unclear> <note>likely a corruption of a name like Hermes or a specific Arabic authority</note>, is the form of a man standing upright on his feet, flying atop a dragon. He watches those below, and in his left hand he holds a shield. Beneath his feet, he has the figure of a dragon. Such is the form.

---

The form of the Sun, according to the opinion of other wise men, is the form of a man standing upright upon a chariot <term>currum</term> <note>a four-wheeled vehicle used in ancient processions or warfare</note> which four horses pull. In his right hand is a mirror <term>speculum</term>, and in his left a shield. All of his garments are saffron-yellow <note>original: "crocee," referring to the color of the crocus flower, associated with the light of the sun</note>. Such is the form.

---

The form of the Sun, according to the opinion of the *Picatrix* <note>The *Picatrix* is a famous medieval grimoire of astrological magic, originally written in Arabic as the *Ghayat al-Hakim*</note>, is the form of a seated king wearing a crown on his head. He has the form of a black raven before him, and beneath his feet is the figure of the sun which we mentioned previously. This is the figure.

---

The form of Venus, according to the opinion of <unclear>Heretis</unclear>, is the form of a woman standing upright on her feet, holding an apple <term>pomum</term> in her right hand. This is the form.

<summary>This page describes and illustrates various symbolic depictions of the Sun and Venus, drawing from diverse astrological traditions including the Picatrix and other "wise men." These figures were often used as visual guides for creating talismans or for meditative practices in celestial magic.</summary>

<keywords>Sun, Venus, Picatrix, planetary forms, astrology, dragon, chariot, saffron, apple, iconography</keywords>
